The jump control is pressed while the player character is standing during active gameplay → The player character leaves the ground and follows an upward jump arc.
The falling player character reaches the ground level during active gameplay → The player character lands with its feet on the ground and stops descending.

The left movement control is held while the player character is at the left edge of the current camera view during active gameplay → The player character stays inside the gameplay view with its left side aligned at the left camera boundary instead of moving off the left edge.

The player character moves beyond 45% of the gameplay view width from the left side during active gameplay → The world scenery and ground scroll left across the canvas while the player character remains visible in the gameplay view.
The on-screen joystick is dragged to the right from its neutral position → The joystick knob is displayed to the right of the center of the joystick base.
The on-screen joystick is released after being dragged away from its neutral position → The joystick knob returns to the center of the joystick base.

The fire control is pressed while the player has the normal weapon ready, is facing right, and is not aiming upward → One projectile appears at the player character and travels to the right across the gameplay area.

The fire control is pressed while the player has the normal weapon ready, is facing left, and is not aiming upward → One projectile appears at the player character and travels to the left across the gameplay area.
The fire control is pressed while the player has the normal weapon ready and is aiming upward → One projectile appears above the player character and travels upward through the gameplay area.

The fire control is pressed while the player has the fan weapon ready and is not aiming upward → Three projectiles appear at the player character in a spread: one travels straight in the facing direction, one travels diagonally upward in that direction, and one travels diagonally downward in that direction.

The fire control is pressed while the player has the fan weapon ready and is aiming upward → Three projectiles appear above the player character in an upward spread: one travels straight upward, one travels diagonally up-left, and one travels diagonally up-right.
A soldier enemy spawn is selected during active gameplay → A dark unicorn enemy appears on the right side of the gameplay area on the ground.
A flying enemy spawn is selected during active gameplay → A winged dark unicorn enemy appears at an elevated position above the ground on the right side of the gameplay area.
A flying enemy is active during gameplay → The winged dark unicorn enemy moves horizontally while its vertical position oscillates up and down.
A boss enemy spawn is selected while the score is above 1200 and no other boss is present → A boss enemy appears on the right side of the gameplay area with a visible health bar above it.
A boss enemy is farther than its stopping distance to the right of the player character during active gameplay → The boss moves left toward the player character while both remain visible.
A non-boss enemy's firing interval is reached while the player character is within its firing range → One enemy projectile appears at the enemy and travels toward the player character.

A boss enemy's firing interval is reached while the player character is within its firing range → Three enemy projectiles appear at the boss: one central projectile and two angled projectiles on either side, all traveling toward the player character.
A player-fired projectile collides with an enemy that survives the hit → The projectile disappears at the enemy and pink hit particles appear at the collision point.

A player-fired projectile defeats a non-boss enemy → The enemy is no longer visible at its collision position, explosion particles are visible at that position, and within 1 second the score readout changes to a value 100 points higher than the score readout visible immediately before the projectile hit.

A player-fired projectile defeats a boss enemy → The boss is no longer visible at its collision position, explosion particles are visible at that position, and within 1 second the score readout changes to a value 500 points higher than the score readout visible immediately before the projectile hit.
An enemy defeat produces a power-up drop → A power-up icon appears at the defeated enemy's position.
A rapid power-up is visible during active gameplay → The power-up is shown as an icon with the letter "R" centered inside it.
A fan-weapon power-up is visible during active gameplay → The power-up is shown as an icon with the letter "S" centered inside it.
A healing power-up is visible during active gameplay → The power-up is shown as an icon with a heart symbol centered inside it.
A power-up is above its resting ground height during active gameplay → The power-up descends toward the ground.
The player character contacts a non-healing power-up during active gameplay → The power-up icon disappears from the gameplay area.

The player character with 70% health or less contacts a healing power-up during active gameplay → The healing power-up icon disappears, and the health bar fill endpoint shifts right by 30% of the full health-bar frame width within 1 second, with a tolerance of ±10% of the full frame width.

The player character with above 70% health contacts a healing power-up during active gameplay → The healing power-up icon disappears, and the health bar fill reaches the full width of the health-bar frame within 1 second.

An enemy projectile collides with the player character while the player has more than 10% health → The enemy projectile disappears, red hit particles appear at the player character, and the health bar fill endpoint shifts left by 10% of the full health-bar frame width within 1 second, with a tolerance of ±5% of the full frame width.

An enemy projectile collides with the player character when the hit reduces player health to zero → The enemy projectile disappears and a menu overlay is shown with the title text "MISSION FAILED!", a subtitle beginning with "Final Score:", and a button labeled "RETRY".

The player character remains in contact with an enemy during active gameplay while the player has more than 30% health → During 1 second of uninterrupted contact, the health bar fill endpoint shifts left by 30% of the full health-bar frame width, with a tolerance of ±10% of the full frame width.

The player character remains in contact with an enemy when the contact damage reduces player health to zero → A menu overlay is shown with the title text "MISSION FAILED!", a subtitle beginning with "Final Score:", and a button labeled "RETRY".
The retry button is activated while the mission-failed menu overlay is visible → The mission-failed menu overlay disappears and a new gameplay run is shown with the HUD visible.

games.summaryZh: A top-down 640-by-360 canvas game where the player guides a small leprechaun marker through a whimsical playfield with flowers, unicorns, a bomber, homing bombs, dust, explosions, and drag-defined patrol regions. The core loop combines directional movement, collision and knock feedback, automated creature and projectile motion, and score changes shown as a six-position binary display, with progression culminating in a score wrap that triggers a temporary game-over overlay.

requirements.zh: The game has completed its initial load and first play-scene initialization → A 640-by-360 landscape gameplay view is rendered with the play scene active; the initial scene includes a small dark-yellow triangular leprechaun marker in the playfield and a six-position binary score display initialized to all zero symbols.

A score increment reaches a binary score digit that is currently displayed as zero before the maximum score is reached → That score digit changes from the zero symbol to the one symbol in the six-position binary score display.

A score increment reaches a binary score digit that is currently displayed as one before the maximum score is reached → That score digit changes from the one symbol to the zero symbol in the six-position binary score display.

A score increment is accepted while the six-position binary score display reads 111111 → The six-position binary score display changes to 000000, and at least one wide light-red horizontal line stroke is drawn across the playfield.

A left movement request is processed during active play while movement input cooldown is inactive → Within 0.5 seconds, the leprechaun marker's center shifts left from its position at the moment the request is accepted.

A right movement request is processed during active play while movement input cooldown is inactive → Within 0.5 seconds, the leprechaun marker's center shifts right from its position at the moment the request is accepted.

An up movement request is processed during active play while movement input cooldown is inactive → Within 0.5 seconds, the leprechaun marker's center shifts upward from its position at the moment the request is accepted.

A down movement request is processed during active play while movement input cooldown is inactive → Within 0.5 seconds, the leprechaun marker's center shifts downward from its position at the moment the request is accepted.

The leprechaun crosses the left playfield boundary while knock flash and movement cooldown are inactive → The leprechaun marker is rendered at the left boundary margin; within 0.5 seconds after the boundary crossing, the marker is shown in at least one dark-yellow frame and at least one distinct flash-color frame.
A score drop is processed while the six-position binary score display contains at least one one symbol → The rightmost one symbol in the six-position binary score display changes to a zero symbol.
A score drop is processed while the six-position binary score display contains no one symbols → The six-position binary score display remains 000000 after the score-drop opportunity.

The leprechaun reaches a flower while knock flash and movement cooldown are inactive → Within 0.5 seconds after reaching the flower, the leprechaun marker is shown in at least one dark-yellow frame and at least one distinct flash-color frame.

The leprechaun reaches a unicorn while knock flash and movement cooldown are inactive → Within 0.5 seconds after reaching the unicorn, the leprechaun marker is shown in at least one dark-yellow frame and at least one distinct flash-color frame.
The plant generator becomes ready while fewer than ten flowers are visible → One new flower marker appears in the playfield, increasing the visible flower count by one.
The plant generator becomes ready while ten flowers are visible → The playfield remains at ten visible flower markers after the generator opportunity.
A drag selection is active during gameplay → A rectangular outline is drawn from the drag start point to the current cursor position.
An active drag selection has an area below 10000 square game units → The drag-selection rectangle is rendered in light red.
A drag selection is released with an area below 10000 square game units → The drag-selection rectangle disappears and no persistent patrol-region rectangle remains from that release.
A drag selection is released with an area of at least 10000 square game units → The drag-selection rectangle is replaced by a persistent patrol-region rectangle in the playfield.

A bomber firing opportunity occurs while at least one unicorn exists, the bomber is within the visible playfield, and the bomber is facing left → A homing bomb projectile appears at the bomber's position.

The bomber reaches its first patrol endpoint → Within 1 second after reaching the first patrol endpoint, the bomber polygon is rendered away from that endpoint and oriented toward the opposite patrol endpoint.

The bomber is active during gameplay update while its current patrol endpoint is not within 60 game units → Within 1 second, the bomber polygon's center is rendered at a different playfield position than it occupied when the update condition began.

A homing bomb projectile is active during gameplay update before exploding → Within 0.5 seconds, the homing bomb projectile's center is rendered at a different playfield position than it occupied when the update condition began.

A homing bomb has less than 1700 milliseconds of life remaining and its speed is below 300 game units per second → The homing bomb projectile disappears from the playfield, and a light-cyan circular explosion flash appears at the projectile's last position.
A male unicorn is in the after-meet state during herd update → That unicorn's polygon is rendered light yellow.
A female unicorn is in the after-meet state during herd update → That unicorn's polygon is rendered light cyan.
A unicorn is active during gameplay update → Within 1 second, that unicorn polygon's center is rendered at a different playfield position than it occupied when the update condition began.
A unicorn is in the after-meet state during herd update while a patrol-region rectangle is visible → The patrol-region rectangle disappears from the playfield.
The game-over display timer is decremented to zero from a positive value during gameplay update → The dense dark-brown game-over line overlay is no longer drawn over the playfield.

A leprechaun knock is accepted while knock flash and movement cooldown are inactive → Within 0.5 seconds after the knock is accepted, the playfield background and entities are rendered at a screen alignment offset from their alignment at the moment of the knock, and the leprechaun marker is shown in at least one dark-yellow frame and at least one distinct flash-color frame.
A leprechaun knock is processed while at least three flowers are visible → The visible flower count decreases by three flower markers.
The leprechaun is moving while fewer than three dust particles are visible → A dust particle appears at the leprechaun's current position.

games.summaryZh: A minimalist arcade arena shooter where the player controls a ring-shaped ship inside a bordered playfield, dodges hostile shapes, aims and fires projectiles, collects ammo, and tries to survive while raising the score. The game begins with an illustrated control-and-instruction screen, moves into a continuous spawn-and-shoot survival loop with HUD score and ammo readouts, and ends in a game-over presentation that can be restarted.

requirements.zh: The game has completed its initial intro screen setup → The intro screen shows the title text "Shooooooot!!", the instruction lines "avoid being hit", "point to shoot", and "max ammo: 404", both "Keyboard and Mouse" and "Gamepad" control panels, and the prompt text "Click or Press Enter to Start".
Enter is pressed while the intro screen is active → The intro screen disappears and the game transitions to the gameplay view.

A new gameplay session has completed initial gameplay scene setup → The playfield shows a rectangular border inset from the canvas edges, the player character appears as a ring at the center of the playfield, the HUD shows "score: 0" near the top-left of the playfield, and the HUD shows ammo text beginning with "ammo: " near the top-right of the playfield.
The Left Arrow key is held during active gameplay while the player character is not at the left edge of the playfield → The player character moves left across the playfield during the key hold.
The Right Arrow key is held during active gameplay while the player character is not at the right edge of the playfield → The player character moves right across the playfield during the key hold.
The Up Arrow key is held during active gameplay while the player character is not at the top edge of the playfield → The player character moves upward across the playfield during the key hold.
The Down Arrow key is held during active gameplay while the player character is not at the bottom edge of the playfield → The player character moves downward across the playfield during the key hold.
The mouse button is held during active gameplay while the player can fire → One or more bullet sprites appear at the player and move from the player toward the mouse pointer position.

The right gamepad thumbstick leaves the aim dead zone during active gameplay while the player can fire → One or more bullet sprites appear at the player and move in the right thumbstick aim direction.

The player fires while single-shot mode is active, the aim is outside the dead zone, and at least 1 ammo is available → One bullet sprite appears at the player, moves in the aim direction, and the ammo text decreases by 1.

The player fires while two-shot mode is active, the aim is outside the dead zone, and at least 2 ammo are available → Two bullet sprites appear at the player, move away from the player in separated directions around the aim direction, and the ammo text decreases by 2.

The player fires while three-shot mode is active, the aim is outside the dead zone, and enough ammo is available for the three-shot volley → Three bullet sprites appear at the player, move away from the player in separated directions around the aim direction, and the ammo text decreases by 3.
The player attempts to fire while the aim is inside the dead zone → No new bullet sprite appears during that fire attempt.
The player attempts to fire in single-shot mode with zero ammo → No new bullet sprite appears during that fire attempt.
The player attempts to fire in two-shot mode with fewer than 2 ammo → No new bullet sprite appears during that fire attempt.

The repeating fire timer reaches its firing interval during active gameplay while a valid firing input remains held and enough ammo is available → A new bullet sprite appears at the player and moves away from the player in the current aim direction.
A player bullet crosses outside the playfield boundary during active gameplay → The bullet sprite is no longer visible in the playfield on the next rendered frame.
A scheduled enemy spawn event fires during active gameplay → At least one new spawn animation appears in the playfield.
A box spawn pattern is triggered during active gameplay → Eight spawn animations appear in a three-by-three arrangement around the player with the center position empty.

A side spawn pattern selects the vertical-sides branch during active gameplay → Five spawn animations appear along the left side of the playfield and five spawn animations appear along the right side of the playfield.
A spawn animation reaches its completion point → The converging spawn particles disappear and the spawned enemy sprite appears at the spawn position.
An enemy spawn roll selects an ammo drop replacement → The spawn animation resolves into an ammo drop sprite.
A spiral enemy is created with a clockwise spin direction → The spiral enemy circle follows a clockwise orbiting path while it remains visible in the playfield.
A hunter enemy updates while the player is present and the hunter is outside one movement step from the player → The hunter enemy moves along a path aimed toward the player's position.
A hunter enemy updates while the player is inside the hunter's repel arc → The hunter enemy changes to a path moving away from the player's position.
A seeker enemy updates while the player is present and the seeker is outside one movement step from the player → The seeker enemy moves along a path aimed toward the player's position.

A spiral enemy updates while the player is present and the spiral's center is outside one movement step from the player → The spiral enemy's rotating center moves along a path aimed toward the player's position.

An asteroid reaches the left boundary of its allowed area while moving left → The asteroid remains inside the playfield border and its motion changes from leftward to rightward on the next rendered frame.
An asteroid is hit while its accumulated hit count is below the asteroid destruction threshold → The asteroid remains visible and the edge of its circular body contracts inward after the hit.
An asteroid is hit when its accumulated hit count reaches the asteroid destruction threshold → The asteroid sprite disappears and a particle blast appears at the asteroid's position.

A non-asteroid enemy with point value 10 begins its first explosion while the player is not exploded → The enemy sprite disappears, a particle blast appears at the enemy's position, and the score text increases by 10.
An unexploded ammo drop is absorbed by the player while the player is not exploded → The ammo drop sprite disappears, the score text increases by 50, and the ammo text increases by 50.

An unexploded ammo drop is absorbed by the player while the player is not exploded and the ammo gain would exceed the ammo maximum → The ammo drop sprite disappears, the score text increases by 50, and the ammo text reads "ammo: 404".
A player bullet overlaps an enemy during active gameplay → The bullet sprite disappears at the collision position.
The player overlaps the playfield boundary during active gameplay → A particle blast appears at the player's position and the player ring disappears.
The player collides with a non-ammo enemy during active gameplay → A particle blast appears at the player position and the player ring disappears.
An enemy overlaps the playfield boundary during active gameplay → The enemy sprite disappears and a particle blast appears at the enemy's position.

The player reaches a game-over state with a score above the stored high score → A game-over overlay is visible with the text "GAME" and "OVER", a message beginning with "New High Score: " and ending with "!!", and the restart prompt "Press Enter or Button 0 to Restart".

The player reaches a game-over state with a score not above the stored high score → A game-over overlay is visible with the text "GAME" and "OVER", a message beginning with "Score to Beat: ", and the restart prompt "Press Enter or Button 0 to Restart".
Enter is pressed while the game-over screen is active → The game-over overlay and restart prompt disappear, and the game transitions back to the gameplay view.

games.summaryZh: A browser-based turn-based ASCII dungeon adventure where the player controls a hero exploring a castle, fighting rats, goblins, orcs, and a dragon. The objective is to survive monster encounters, gain experience through combat, rest when needed, and defeat the dragon to win. Play centers on keyboard-driven tile movement, adjacent attacks, visible console feedback, and simple progression shown in the side panel.

requirements.zh: The game presentation canvas has completed creation during initial page setup → A single game canvas with an 800-by-600 presentation area is present on the page.

The main menu stage is rendered → The menu screen shows the story text "Welcome back hero," and "You must fight those monsters and win back our castle.", along with the instructions "Use arrow keys to move." and "Use space bar to rest."
The main menu stage receives an Enter input → The menu screen is replaced by the adventure gameplay view.

The adventure stage receives an Arrow Up input while the hero can accept a new action and the destination tile is walkable and unoccupied → The hero sprite walks one map step toward the top of the gameplay view.

The adventure stage receives an Arrow Down input while the hero can accept a new action and the destination tile is walkable and unoccupied → The hero sprite walks one map step toward the bottom of the gameplay view.

The adventure stage receives an Arrow Left input while the hero can accept a new action and the destination tile is walkable and unoccupied → The hero sprite walks one map step toward the left side of the gameplay view.

The adventure stage receives an Arrow Right input while the hero can accept a new action and the destination tile is walkable and unoccupied → The hero sprite walks one map step toward the right side of the gameplay view.

The adventure stage receives a Space input while the hero can accept a new action → The hero sprite stays on its current map tile and the gameplay console displays a new message naming the hero and saying "rest for" followed by a numeric healing amount and "hp".

The hero performs an attack against a living non-dragon enemy and the enemy survives the hit → The gameplay console displays a new hit message naming the hero and the target and saying "for" followed by a numeric damage amount.

The hero performs an attack against a living non-dragon enemy and the hit kills the enemy → The gameplay console displays a new hit message for the attack and a new message naming the target and saying "is dead".

The hero performs an attack against the living dragon and the dragon survives the hit → The gameplay console displays a new hit message naming the hero and the dragon and saying "for" followed by a numeric damage amount.
The hero performs an attack against the dragon and the hit kills the dragon → The adventure gameplay view is replaced by the victory screen.
An actor attacks a living target with an attack result that deals 0 damage after defense → The gameplay console displays a new hit message naming the attacker and target and saying "for 0 damage".

A non-hero actor adjacent to the hero receives an AI turn with no queued action → The gameplay console displays a new hit message naming that actor and the hero and saying "for" followed by a numeric damage amount.
A non-hero actor attacks the living hero with damage after defense greater than the hero's current HP → The adventure gameplay view is replaced by the game over screen.
The adventure stage begins an update while the hero is dead → The adventure gameplay view is replaced by the game over screen.
A non-hero actor performs a walk action to the north toward a walkable unoccupied destination → That actor's sprite moves one map step toward the top of the gameplay view.
The hero performs a walk action to the north toward a non-walkable destination with no attackable actor there → The hero sprite remains on its current map tile.
The hero performs a walk action to the north toward a tile occupied by a living actor → The hero sprite remains on its current map tile.

The hero performs an attack against a living target that survives the hit while the hero's pre-attack XP is at least 2 points below the current next-level XP requirement → In the right-side information panel, the XP line's numerator increases by 1 from its pre-attack displayed value and the XP line's denominator stays the same.

The hero performs an attack that kills a living non-dragon enemy while the hero's pre-attack XP is at least 4 points below the current next-level XP requirement → In the right-side information panel, the XP line's numerator increases by 3 from its pre-attack displayed value and the XP line's denominator stays the same.
The adventure gameplay view is rendered while the hero actor is inside the current map viewport → A white "@" glyph is drawn at the hero's map tile in the map area.
The adventure gameplay view is rendered while a rat actor is inside the current map viewport → A grey lowercase "r" glyph is drawn at that rat's map tile in the map area.
The adventure gameplay view is rendered while a goblin actor is inside the current map viewport → A brown lowercase "g" glyph is drawn at that goblin's map tile in the map area.
The adventure gameplay view is rendered while an orc actor is inside the current map viewport → A light-brown uppercase "O" glyph is drawn at that orc's map tile in the map area.
The adventure gameplay view is rendered while the dragon actor is inside the current map viewport → A red uppercase "D" glyph is drawn at the dragon's map tile in the map area.
A map cell with value 0 is rendered inside the adventure map viewport → That map tile is drawn as a dark-blue terrain glyph.
The adventure gameplay view renders the right-side information panel → A vertical column of "|" glyphs is drawn at the left edge of the right-side information panel.

The adventure gameplay view renders its console border → A horizontal row of "-" glyphs spans the top of the console area, with one "+" glyph at the divider between the map area and the right-side information panel.
The game over stage is rendered → A bordered message box is visible with a top border reading "+-------------+" and a line containing "GAME OVER".
The game over stage receives an Enter input → The displayed game over screen is replaced by the opening menu screen.
The game won stage is rendered → A five-line bordered message box is visible, with the middle line containing the text "You won !".
The game won stage receives an Enter input → The displayed victory screen is replaced by the opening menu screen.

games.summaryZh: Prism Paddock is a cozy browser gardening and caretaking game about helping a unicorn restore a lost rainbow. The player enters a tiled grass paddock, unlocks rainbow colors, drags color swatches to feed the unicorn, cleans the resulting butterfly-poop to earn colored butterflies, and spends those butterflies on decorative plants. Progression comes from unlocking new colors and shop items, arranging decorations to satisfy unicorn quests, and ultimately restoring the full rainbow while continuing to decorate the paddock.

requirements.zh: The page has completed its initial load before the player enters the game section → A start screen is visible with the title text “Prism Paddock” and a link labeled “Click to start”.
The player activates the “Click to start” link on the start screen → The game section is shown instead of the start screen, with the paddock play area and unicorn visible.
The gameplay view has completed paddock grid setup → The paddock is visible as a rectangular grass board with 9 columns and 7 rows of square tiles, and the unicorn is positioned on the center tile.
The first-time intro tutorial begins in the game section → A comic speech bubble is shown with the text “Oh, hello there! I've been waiting for you!”.

The player clicks the unicorn while no rainbow color has been unlocked → A red color swatch appears in the bottom palette, and the palette shows the instruction “Drag a color onto the unicorn to feed her.”
The scheduled feeding tutorial prompt fires after the red color has been unlocked → A tutorial speech bubble appears beside the unicorn prompting the player to drag a color onto the unicorn.

The gameplay view is rendered while at least one rainbow color is unlocked and at least one cleaned item has been counted → A top status bar is visible showing butterfly-count entries for the unlocked rainbow colors.
The gameplay background is rendered after two rainbow colors have been unlocked → The page background behind the paddock is a diagonal gradient with visible red and orange color bands.
The bottom palette is rendered with at least one locked rainbow color → Locked color swatches are shown as dimmed grayscale swatches with no selected-swatch outline or glow.
The bottom palette is rendered after at least two rainbow colors have been unlocked → The right-side palette help text reads “Tap a color to shop with it.”

The player begins a real drag from an enabled color swatch while the unicorn is not digesting → A floating color fragment appears under the pointer, and the unicorn changes to a frozen anticipation pose.
The player releases a dragged color fragment over the unicorn → The floating color fragment disappears, and the bottom help text changes to “Wait for the unicorn to finish!”.
The player releases a dragged color fragment away from the unicorn → The floating color fragment disappears, and the bottom help text remains “Drag a color onto the unicorn to feed her.”
The player presses an enabled color swatch while the bottom help text says “Wait for the unicorn to finish!” → No floating color fragment appears.
The player presses a locked color swatch in the bottom palette while the unicorn is not digesting → No floating color fragment appears under the pointer.
The unicorn finishes the chewing interval after an accepted color fragment and a free destination tile exists → The unicorn begins walking away from its current tile toward another grass tile.
The unicorn reaches its poop destination after being fed → A butterfly-poop appears on the tile the unicorn was occupying, and the unicorn steps onto an adjacent tile.
A normal butterfly-poop is rendered on a grass tile → The butterfly-poop sprite is shown on the tile with a small butterfly icon over it.
A rainbow butterfly-poop is rendered on a grass tile → The butterfly-poop sprite is shown on the tile with rainbow coloring and no small butterfly icon over it.

The first butterfly-poop has appeared and the unicorn finishes stepping away from it → The unicorn shows a shocked pose and a speech bubble appears with the text “Oops... I made a butterfly-poop... Can you clean it up, please?”.
The player clicks a grass tile containing butterfly-poop → The butterfly-poop disappears from that tile and butterfly icons fly from that tile toward the top status bar.
The player cleans a non-rainbow butterfly-poop → Three butterfly icons fly from the cleaned tile toward the matching color counter in the top status bar.
The player cleans a rainbow butterfly-poop → Butterfly icons fly from the cleaned tile toward every visible color counter in the top status bar.

The first butterfly-poop cleanup is completed → A speech bubble appears with the text “Thank you! Cleaning a butterfly-poop gives you butterflies back! You can spend them to make the surroundings prettier!”.

A color-counter butterfly flight finishes after a cleanup reward → Within 1 second after the flight icon reaches the destination counter, the number beside that counter equals the number shown immediately before the cleanup plus 3.
The player taps an enabled color swatch when the shop is available → A shop panel with plant item cards is shown, along with the instruction “Drag an item onto the grass to place it.”

The player taps a different enabled color swatch in the bottom palette while the shop panel is open → The selected-swatch highlight moves to the tapped color swatch and the shop panel remains visible.

The shop panel is rendered after butterflies have been harvested but before any flower decoration has been placed → The shop panel shows a Flower item card, and no Mushroom or Crystal item card is visible.

The shop panel is rendered after at least one flower decoration has been placed and before blue has been unlocked → The shop panel shows Flower and Mushroom item cards, and no Crystal item card is visible.
The shop panel is rendered after blue has been unlocked and at least one flower decoration has been placed → The shop panel shows Flower, Mushroom, and Crystal item cards.
The shop panel is rendered with an item card whose selected-color butterfly count is below that item’s cost → That unaffordable item card is shown in grayscale and translucent styling.

The player begins pressing a shop item card whose selected-color butterfly count is below that item’s cost → No dragged plant sprite appears under the pointer and no plant placement preview appears on the grass.
The player begins a real drag from an enabled shop item card → A floating plant sprite matching the selected shop item appears under the pointer.
The player begins a real drag from an enabled shop item card onto a valid grass tile → A plant placement preview appears on the target grass tile.
The player drags a shop item over the tile occupied by the unicorn → No plant placement preview is shown on the unicorn’s tile.
The player drags a shop item over a tile containing butterfly-poop → No plant placement preview is shown on the butterfly-poop tile.

The player drags a shop item over a grass tile that already contains a decoration → The plant placement preview appears on that tile and the existing decoration on that tile is hidden while the preview is visible.
The player releases a dragged shop item while its placement preview is on a valid grass tile → The placement preview is replaced by a placed plant decoration on that grass tile.
The player releases a dragged shop item on a grass tile that already contains a decoration → The old decoration disappears from that tile and is replaced by the newly placed decoration.
The player releases a dragged shop item when no valid grass-tile placement preview is visible → No new plant decoration is added to the grass.
A placed flower decoration is rendered after its placement pop-in animation has completed → A flower decoration is visible on its grass tile.
A placed mushroom decoration is rendered after its placement pop-in animation has completed → A mushroom decoration is visible on its grass tile.
A placed crystal decoration is rendered after its placement pop-in animation has completed → A crystal decoration is visible on its grass tile.
The first green quest begins → A quest speech bubble appears beside the unicorn with the text “Huh, green didn't unlock... What can we do?”.
The active green quest is started with its full required lineup on the board → The required plant decorations for the quest are highlighted on the grass.
The violet quest begins → A quest speech bubble appears beside the unicorn, and the required plant decorations for the violet sequence are highlighted on the grass.
The player clicks the currently highlighted correct decoration during an active quest before the last required step → The highlight moves to the next required decoration in the quest sequence.
The player clicks a nonmatching decoration after making progress in an active quest → The quest highlight resets to the first required decoration in the sequence.

The player clicks the final highlighted correct decoration in an active quest sequence → The quest speech bubble is not visible, and a glowing rainbow arc overlay with centered unlock text is visible over the game view.
A rainbow color beyond the initial red becomes newly unlocked through progression → A glowing rainbow arc overlay spans the game view, with centered text naming that color followed by “unlocked!”.
A rainbow color unlock celebration finishes landing on its palette swatch → The newly unlocked color swatch in the bottom palette is shown in full color instead of dimmed grayscale.
The green unlock celebration finishes → A speech bubble sequence begins beside the unicorn with the text “I'd never have figured that out on my own!”.
The blue unlock celebration finishes → A speech bubble appears with the text “They say there are magic crystals that draw their power from the sea... Can you believe that?”.
The final violet rainbow color becomes newly unlocked → A color-unlock celebration is shown and confetti pieces burst across the game view.

The final violet unlock speech begins → A speech bubble appears with the text “Wow, you've completely restored the rainbow, thank you so much!” followed by “If you feel like it, you can keep decorating my surroundings however you please.” on the next line.
The unicorn selects a left-adjacent tile during an idle wander step → The unicorn moves one grass tile to the left and faces left.
The player clicks the unicorn when it is idle and a previous speech line is available → The unicorn stops on its tile and a speech bubble appears replaying the previous line.

games.summaryZh: Dewdrop Farm is a small browser farming game about tending a grid of plots through seasons, growing crops, handling visiting animals, and using harvests and sales to progress. The player switches between tending, buying, selling, and information screens, selects tools or inventory slots, tills and waters soil, plants seeds, buys supplies, harvests crops, sells inventory, and gains experience toward higher farm levels that unlock additional crops and improve luck.

requirements.zh: The initial page markup is presented before any player interaction → The title text "Dewdrop Farm" and a "New Game" control are visible in the UI.
The game finishes its initial startup rendering → The tend screen control is highlighted as active, the farm area is visible, and the store and market areas are hidden.

The player switches to the tend screen while another screen is selected → The tend screen control is highlighted as active, the farm area is visible, the farm information panel is hidden, and the store and market areas are hidden.

The player switches to the buy screen while another screen is selected → The buy screen control is highlighted as active, the store area is visible, the farm information panel is hidden, and the farm and market areas are hidden.

The player switches to the sell screen while another screen is selected → The sell screen control is highlighted as active, the market area is visible, the farm information panel is hidden, and the farm and store areas are hidden.

The player switches to the geek screen while another screen is selected → The geek screen control is highlighted as active, the farm information panel is visible, and the farm, store, and market areas are hidden.

The player activates the New Game control after the game is running → The tend screen control is highlighted as active, the hoe tool control is highlighted as active, the farm area is visible, and the store and market areas are hidden.

The player activates the New Game control after the farm information panel shows nonzero experience or a level above zero → The farm information panel shows "Level: 0" and an Experience line whose current value is 0 after the reset render.
The player selects the hoe tool while a different tool is selected → The hoe tool control is highlighted as active and the water and seed-slot tool controls are not highlighted as active.
The player selects the water tool while a different tool is selected → The water tool control is highlighted as active and the hoe and seed-slot tool controls are not highlighted as active.

The player selects the first seed-slot tool while a different tool is selected → The first seed-slot control is highlighted as active and the hoe, water, and other seed-slot controls are not highlighted as active.
The farm grid is rendered for a farm with six rows and six columns → The farm area displays 36 plot tiles arranged as six rows and six columns.
The cash display is rendered for the current farm state → A numeric cash value is visible next to a coin tile icon.
The tool inventory bar is rendered from the page markup → A hoe tool icon with key label "1", a watering-can tool icon with key label "2", and four seed-slot boxes are visible in one inventory row.

The farm information panel is rendered for the current farm state → The panel shows the current year with an ordinal suffix, a "Level:" line, an "Experience:" line formatted as current experience slash needed experience, and a "Luck:" line ending with a percent sign.

The buy screen renders a crop whose required level is above the player's current level and whose crop type is not wildflower → That store entry displays the name line "404 Not Found" and an unlock line stating the crop name followed by "available at Level" and the required level number.
The buy screen renders a crop that is available at the player's current level → That store entry displays the crop name as the name line instead of "404 Not Found".
The buy screen renders during winter → The store area includes a wildflower seed entry displayed by name.
The sell screen renders when the player has no crops or seeds available to sell → The market area shows the message "It looks like you don't have any crops to sell. You can use seeds to grow crops."
A seed inventory item with an amount above zero is rendered in a tool slot → The item picture contains a seed packet icon, a small crop sprite for the seed type, and an amount sticker.
A non-seed inventory item with an amount above zero is rendered in a tool slot → The item picture contains the item sprite without a seed packet icon and includes an amount sticker.
A farm plot containing ground, fertilizer, water, and a planted crop is rendered → The fertilizer tile, blue water overlay, and crop sprite are all visible within the same plot square.
The player uses the hoe tool on an empty farm plot that is not tilled → That plot changes from plain ground to a tilled soil tile after the next render.
The player uses the water tool on a tilled farm plot that is not already watered → A blue water overlay appears on that tilled plot after the next render.
The player uses the water tool on a farm plot that is not tilled → That plot does not gain a blue water overlay and its visible contents match the pre-use appearance after the next render.

The player uses a seed-slot tool containing exactly one seed item on a tilled plot with no planted crop → A crop sprite for that seed's crop appears on the target plot, and the used seed-slot becomes empty after the next render.

The player uses a seed-slot tool containing a seed item on an untilled plot → No crop sprite appears on the target plot, and the used seed-slot keeps the same visible seed icon and amount as before the use.

The player uses a seed-slot tool containing a seed item on a plot that already has a planted crop → The existing crop sprite remains on the target plot, and the used seed-slot keeps the same visible seed icon and amount as before the use.

The player uses a seed-slot tool containing exactly one fertilizer on a tilled plot that is not fertilized → A fertilizer tile appears on the target plot, and the used inventory slot becomes empty after the next render.

The player uses a seed-slot tool containing fertilizer on an untilled plot → No fertilizer tile appears on the target plot, and the used inventory slot keeps the same visible fertilizer icon and amount as before the use.

The player uses a seed-slot tool containing fertilizer on a plot that is already fertilized → The target plot keeps one visible fertilizer tile, and the used inventory slot keeps the same visible fertilizer icon and amount as before the use.

The player uses a seed-slot tool containing exactly one cow item while an animal is visible on the farm → The visible animal sprite is rendered as a cow instead of a bunny, and the used inventory slot becomes empty after the next render.

The player harvests a mature non-sprinkler crop while there is inventory space and no matching crop item is already visible in the sellable inventory → The mature crop sprite disappears from the plot, and a corresponding crop item appears in the sellable inventory after the next render.
The player harvests an immature crop → The crop sprite remains on the plot with the same visible growth stage after the next render.
The player harvests a sprinkler plant → The sprinkler sprite remains on the plot after the next render.
The player harvests a mature crop when the inventory cannot accept the harvested crop item → The mature crop sprite remains on the plot after the next render.
The player uses the hoe tool on an immature planted crop → The crop sprite disappears from the target plot after the next render.

The player uses the hoe tool on a newly planted minimum-stage crop while there is inventory space and no matching seed item is already visible in a seed-slot inventory control → The crop sprite disappears from the target plot, and a seed item for that crop appears in a seed-slot inventory control after the next render.

The player buys an available seed item while there is enough cash, inventory space, and no matching seed item is already visible in the seed-slot inventory controls → A seed item for that crop appears in a seed-slot inventory control, and the cash display decreases by the store entry's visible price after the next render.

The player buys an available seed item while there is enough cash, inventory space, and a matching seed item is already visible in the seed-slot inventory controls → The matching seed item's visible amount increases by 1, and the cash display decreases by the store entry's visible price after the next render.

The player tries to buy a crop whose required level is above the player's current level and whose crop type is not wildflower → The visible seed-slot inventory controls keep the same icons and amount stickers as before the buy attempt.

The player tries to buy an available seed item without enough cash → The visible seed-slot inventory controls keep the same icons and amount stickers as before the buy attempt, and the cash display keeps the same number as before the buy attempt.

The player tries to buy an available seed item when the inventory cannot accept the seed item → The visible seed-slot inventory controls keep the same icons and amount stickers as before the buy attempt, and the cash display keeps the same number as before the buy attempt.

The player sells an inventory item that is listed in the market with visible amount 1 → That market entry disappears, and the cash display increases by the market entry's visible price after the next render.

The player sells an inventory item that is listed in the market with visible amount at least 2 → That market item's visible amount decreases by 1, and the cash display increases by the market entry's visible price after the next render.
A farm plot containing the animal entity is rendered while the farm is not in cow mode → The plot shows a bunny animal sprite.
A farm plot containing the animal entity is rendered while the farm is in cow mode → The plot shows a cow animal sprite.
The game update creates a bunny when no bunny is on the farm and the bunny timer has expired → A bunny animal sprite appears on an interior farm plot after the update render.

The player pokes a visible bunny on an interior farm plot with the hand interaction → The bunny sprite disappears from its original plot and appears on a plot sharing an edge or corner with the original plot, and the farm information panel's Experience value increases by 15 after the next render, up to the visible maximum shown for that level.

The player pokes a visible cow on an interior farm plot with the hand interaction → The cow sprite disappears from its original plot and appears on a plot sharing an edge or corner with the original plot, and the farm information panel's Experience value increases by 15 after the next render, up to the visible maximum shown for that level.

The player pokes a visible bunny on an interior farm plot with the hoe interaction when the fertilizer reward check does not succeed → The bunny sprite disappears from its original plot and appears on a plot sharing an edge or corner with the original plot, and the farm information panel's Experience value decreases by 20 after the next render, down to 0 if fewer than 20 experience points were shown before the poke.

The player pokes a visible cow on an interior farm plot with the hoe interaction when the fertilizer reward check does not succeed → The cow sprite disappears from its original plot and appears on a plot sharing an edge or corner with the original plot, and the farm information panel's Experience value decreases by 20 after the next render, down to 0 if fewer than 20 experience points were shown before the poke.

The player pokes a visible bunny on an interior farm plot with the hoe interaction when the fertilizer reward check succeeds → The bunny sprite disappears from its original plot, no animal sprite appears on a plot sharing an edge or corner with the original plot after the next render, and the farm information panel's Experience value decreases by 20 after the next render, down to 0 if fewer than 20 experience points were shown before the poke.

The player pokes a visible cow on an interior farm plot with the hoe interaction when the fertilizer reward check succeeds → The cow sprite disappears from its original plot, no animal sprite appears on a plot sharing an edge or corner with the original plot after the next render, and the farm information panel's Experience value decreases by 20 after the next render, down to 0 if fewer than 20 experience points were shown before the poke.
The player pokes a visible bunny or cow on an edge farm plot with the hand interaction → The animal sprite disappears from that edge plot after the next render.
The player feeds a visible cow with exactly one crop item after at least one in-game day since the previous feeding → The fed crop item's inventory entry disappears after the next render.

The automatic animal hop update processes a visible bunny whose hop timer has elapsed and whose last feeding was not today or yesterday → The bunny sprite disappears from its original plot and appears on a plot sharing an edge with the original plot after the update render.

The automatic animal hop update processes a visible cow whose hop timer has elapsed and whose last feeding was not today or yesterday → The cow sprite disappears from its original plot and appears on a plot sharing an edge with the original plot after the update render.
A cow-mode animal moves onto a plot containing a non-sprinkler crop → A cow sprite appears on that plot, and the crop sprite that was on the plot is no longer visible after the move render.
A cow-mode animal moves onto a plot containing a sprinkler plant → A cow sprite appears on that plot, and the sprinkler sprite remains visible on the same plot after the move render.

The automatic growth update processes a planted crop that is ready to grow during one of its growing seasons → The crop sprite changes from its previous growth stage to the next growth-stage sprite after the update render.
The automatic growth update processes a planted crop that is ready to grow outside its growing seasons → The crop sprite changes to a dead or withered crop sprite after the update render.

The automatic growth eligibility check processes a planted crop whose alive days are below the required days for its current stage → The crop sprite keeps the same growth-stage appearance after the update render.
The automatic update drains a plot that was watered on an earlier in-game day → The plot's blue water overlay disappears after the update render.
The automatic drain eligibility check processes a plot watered during the current in-game day → The plot keeps its blue water overlay after the update render.
The automatic update processes an empty tilled plot that should revert to grass → The plot loses its tilled-soil texture and any blue water overlay after the update render.

The automatic sprinkler update processes a planted sprinkler that is due to water and has tilled plots in its surrounding neighborhood → A blue water overlay appears on the sprinkler's plot and on each tilled neighboring plot in the surrounding neighborhood after the update render.

The automatic time update advances the farm into the next in-game day within the same season → The time display changes from the previous day number to the next day number while keeping the same season name after the update render.

The automatic time update advances the farm from the final day of a season into the first day of the next season → The time display changes to the next season name with day number 1 after the update render.

The player harvests a mature tomato while there is inventory space for the tomato item and the farm information panel's Experience current value is below the displayed needed value → A tomato item is visible in the sellable inventory, a tomato crop sprite remains on the plot in a non-mature growth stage, and the farm information panel's Experience current value increases by 12 after the next render, capped at the displayed needed value.

The player harvests a mature potato while there is inventory space for the potato item and the farm information panel's Experience current value is below the displayed needed value → The mature potato sprite disappears from the plot, a potato item is visible in the sellable inventory, and the farm information panel's Experience current value increases by 14 after the next render, capped at the displayed needed value.

An experience-rewarding action raises the farm across exactly one level threshold → The farm information panel's Level value increases by 1 after the next render, the Experience line shows the new current experience against the new needed value, and the Luck line changes to a percent value 2 percentage points higher than before.

games.summaryZh: A dark, minimalist card-based incremental board game where the player builds a grid of occult cards, spends death energy to buy new ranks of cards, drags cards to rearrange or merge matching pairs, and activates card abilities to generate or modify resources. The objective is to progress by leveling card ranks, unlocking stronger or special cards, expanding the board, and using sacrifice or restart mechanics for longer-term soul-power advancement. Interaction is primarily pointer or touch based, with desktop hover feedback, drag-and-drop movement, mobile move/use mode switching, and optional autoplay for repeated card activation.

requirements.zh: The game is in the suspended no-update screen state → The current gameplay view is drawn with the centered prompt text "Click on the Screen to Continue the Game" visible near the lower part of the play area.

The player clicks or taps the suspended no-update screen while the continue prompt is being shown → The prompt text "Click on the Screen to Continue the Game" is no longer visible, and the gameplay view is shown without the suspended-screen overlay.

The player right-clicks a card when the Harvest interaction is available for that card → The death energy value shown in the game UI changes to a higher number than its pre-interaction number, and cards shown in a dead or inactive visual state are drawn again in their active card state.

A new card is created for a rank whose current rank level is above that card's existing level → The created card is drawn with the current rank level value, and its displayed skill-number text reflects that rank level.
Two compatible selected cards are merged → The surviving card is drawn with its level increased by 1, and its displayed skill-number text changes to the merged value.
The game starts while no saved game record is available → The board begins with a single starting card visible in the play area, and the resource counters are shown in their new-game starting state.
An unlocked empty board cell is rendered → The cell is drawn as an empty card slot with a visible "+" symbol inside it.
A locked empty board cell is rendered → The cell is drawn as an empty card slot without a visible "+" symbol inside it.
The player begins dragging a movable card while card movement is allowed → The selected card is drawn away from its grid slot and follows the pointer position over the board.
A dragged card is held over an unlocked empty destination cell → The destination cell is outlined with a white rectangular border.
A dragged card is held over a compatible twin card that can be merged → The target card cell is outlined with a red rectangular border.
A dragged eligible special card is held over a Necromancer card that can shatter it → The Necromancer target cell is outlined with a red rectangular border.
The player releases a dragged card over an unlocked empty destination cell → The card is drawn settled in the destination cell, and its previous board cell no longer contains that card.
The player releases a dragged card without a valid empty destination cell or valid target card → The card is drawn back in its original board cell on the next frame.

The player drops an eligible special card onto a Necromancer card while shattering is allowed → The dropped card is no longer drawn in its board cell, and the BUILT UP ENERGY display changes from its pre-drop number.

The player activates the RANK I CARD purchase button while the displayed death energy is at least the displayed cost and an unlocked board cell is available → A new card appears in a board cell that was empty immediately before activation, the DEATH ENERGY display shows a numeric value below its immediately pre-activation value, and the RANK I CARD numeric cost text is different from its immediately pre-activation text.

The player activates the RANK II CARD purchase button while the displayed death energy is at least the displayed cost and an unlocked board cell is available → A new card appears in a board cell that was empty immediately before activation, the DEATH ENERGY display shows a numeric value below its immediately pre-activation value, and the RANK II CARD numeric cost text is different from its immediately pre-activation text.

The player activates the RANK III CARD purchase button while the displayed death energy is at least the displayed cost and an unlocked board cell is available → A new special-rank card appears in a board cell that was empty immediately before activation, the DEATH ENERGY display shows a numeric value below its immediately pre-activation value, and the RANK III CARD button display is different from its immediately pre-activation display.

The player activates a rank purchase button while the displayed death energy is below that button's displayed cost → No new card appears on the board, and the DEATH ENERGY number remains the same through the next rendered frame.

The player activates a rank purchase button when the board is at its card capacity for that purchase state → No new card appears on the board, and the DEATH ENERGY number remains the same through the next rendered frame.
A rank purchase slot has no further purchasable card available → That rank purchase button displays the text "MAX" instead of a numeric cost.
A purchase unlocks the board-expanding special rank card → Previously locked empty card slots change into empty card slots with visible "+" symbols.
A rank receives its third qualifying level-up credit from merging → The roman numeral shown above that rank's purchase button advances by one numeral from its pre-credit display.
A card with a current rank and level that maps to a star pattern is rendered → Plus-sign markers are drawn around the card frame in that card's current star pattern.
A Blood-type card is created → The created Blood-type card is drawn with blood-stain pixel markings on it.

The player activates a Blood-type card while at least one eligible neighboring card is in its blood-transfer range → Blood-stain pixel markings appear on at least one neighboring card in range, and the activated Blood-type card no longer shows its transferred stain set.

The player activates a Blood-type card while no eligible neighboring card is in its blood-transfer range → The activated Blood-type card no longer shows its blood-stain pixel markings, and no neighboring card gains blood-stain markings during the next rendered second.

The player activates a death-energy multiplier card with an eligible non-Necromancer neighboring card in a marked direction → The neighboring card's skill-number text is different from its immediately pre-activation text, and that skill-number text is drawn in red.

The player activates a death-energy transfer card with an eligible non-Necromancer neighboring card in a marked direction → The neighboring card's skill-number text is different from its immediately pre-activation text, and that skill-number text is drawn in red.
The player activates a death-energy multiplier card with an eligible Necromancer neighboring card in a marked direction → The BUILT UP ENERGY number changes from its pre-activation value.
The player activates a death-energy transfer card with an eligible Necromancer neighboring card in a marked direction → The BUILT UP ENERGY number changes from its pre-activation value.
An accepted card activation begins its use animation → The activated card is covered by a red rectangular overlay for the use animation frames.
A no-move blockade state is rendered → A red rectangular outline is drawn around the main board area.
The player tries to drag a card while the no-move blockade state is active → No card is displaced from its board cell during the attempted drag.
The pointer remains over the same card until the card-description delay has elapsed → The card description text appears in the information area of the UI.
The mobile UI is rendered while move-card mode is off → The mobile mode button displays the text "MOVE CARDS".
The mobile UI is rendered while move-card mode is on → The mobile mode button displays the text "USE CARDS".
The player activates the mobile move-mode button while move-card mode is off and the board is not blockaded → The mobile mode button text changes from "MOVE CARDS" to "USE CARDS".
The player activates the mobile move-mode button while move-card mode is on and the board is not blockaded → The mobile mode button text changes from "USE CARDS" to "MOVE CARDS".

The player completes the fourth reset-button activation before the reset counter expires → The board resets to a new-game layout with a single starting card visible and the previous board cards removed.

The player completes the fourth accepted activation of the restart/sacrifice card → The board resets to a single starting card, the previous board cards are removed, and the SOUL POWER display changes from its pre-activation value.
A manual activation enables autoplay → Within one second after the manual activation, at least two red use overlays appear on cards without further pointer input.
A manual activation disables autoplay → No new red use overlay appears on any card without another pointer input during the next rendered second.
A Demon-eye card is rendered while the pointer is to the right of that card → The eye pixels inside the card portrait are offset toward the right side of the portrait.
A rank-I card is rendered in its normal active card state → The card frame contains one white rectangular outline around the portrait area.
A rank-II card is rendered in its normal active card state → The card frame contains two nested white rectangular outlines around the portrait area.
A rank-III card is rendered in its normal active card state → The card frame contains three nested white rectangular outlines around the portrait area.
A special-rank card is rendered in its normal active card state → The card frame contains four nested white rectangular outlines around the portrait area.
The Necromancer card is activated while a Blood-type card is awaiting blood restoration → Blood-stain pixel markings reappear on the Blood-type card.
The UI is rendered while soul power is above zero and built-up energy is at its baseline value of 1 → The BUILT UP ENERGY number shows the same numeric value as the SOUL POWER display.

games.summaryZh: A pixel-art idle/incremental game about a galloping unicorn chasing a leprechaun's pot of gold beneath a rainbow. The player watches coins spawn and get collected for gold, spends gold on upgrades in a modal panel, and eventually unlocks a Catch the Rainbow finale that grants permanent Stubbornness choices. Interaction is primarily through on-screen buttons and modal dialogs, with persistent run progress, reset confirmation, responsive layout changes, and a looping animated fantasy landscape.

requirements.zh: The game completes initial startup with no unresolved Stubbornness choice in saved progress → The game shows the pixel-art play scene on the canvas with no loading overlay text, the GOLD HUD is visible, the Spend Gold button is visible, and the New Game control shows ↺.

The game completes startup with an unresolved Stubbornness point in saved progress → A centered Stubbornness dialog is visible with the title Radiant Resolve, an ATTEMPTS counter area, and the gameplay HUD controls are not visible.

The player activates the Spend Gold control during active running play → A centered upgrade panel appears over a darkened backdrop, the upgrade content is visible, and the gameplay HUD and Spend Gold control are not visible.

The player activates the close control in the open upgrade panel → Within 0.2 seconds, the upgrade panel and its dark backdrop are not visible, and the gameplay HUD and Spend Gold control are visible again.

The player activates the scroll cue control while the upgrade panel is open and its upgrade list has additional content below the visible area → The visible upgrade list content scrolls downward, revealing lower upgrade rows within the same open panel.

The upgrade panel is opened while its upgrade list has content below the visible area → A scroll cue is visible at the bottom of the upgrade panel, including a band over the lower list edge and small sparkle icons.
The player activates the New Game control during active running play while no New Game confirmation is armed → The New Game control changes from ↺ to !.
An armed New Game confirmation reaches its four-second timeout without a second activation → The New Game control changes from ! back to ↺.

The player activates the New Game control while the New Game confirmation is armed and saving succeeds → The run returns to a fresh visible state: the GOLD HUD reads 0 and the New Game control shows ↺.

The player activates the New Game control while the game is in the throw phase of the catch cinematic → The New Game control remains ↺ and the catch cinematic stays on screen without switching to a fresh run.
The catch sequence is in its throw phase and the boot animation is rendered → A boot sprite is visible rotating as it travels along an arc across the gameplay scene.

The catch sequence changes from the throw phase into the tumble phase → The boot is no longer visible, and the unicorn sprite is shown rotating in quarter-turn orientations during the tumble animation.
The catch cinematic completes its tumble phase → The Stubbornness dialog opens over the gameplay scene and the Spend Gold control is not visible.

The player activates a legal Stubbornness choice while the Stubbornness dialog has exactly one available point and saving succeeds → The Stubbornness dialog closes and the active gameplay HUD with the Spend Gold control becomes visible again.
The player activates a legal Stubbornness choice while the Stubbornness dialog has more than one available point and saving succeeds → The Stubbornness dialog remains visible for another choice.
The player presses Escape while the Stubbornness dialog is open with an unresolved point → The Stubbornness dialog remains visible and continues blocking the gameplay HUD controls.

One second of update time elapses while the Stubbornness dialog is open with an unresolved point → The Stubbornness dialog remains visible with its choice rows, the gameplay HUD controls remain hidden, and no new gold coin launches from the pot during that one-second interval.

The Stubbornness dialog is rendered with at least one available choice → Each visible choice row is arranged with a small flag icon on the left, descriptive copy in the middle, and a Choose button on the right.

The Stubbornness dialog is rendered with one permanent trait already at its cap while at least one unresolved point remains → The capped trait's Choose button is visibly disabled with reduced opacity, while the dialog remains open for the unresolved point.

The Stubbornness dialog is rendered with the Weaponised Optimism permanent trait below its cap → The dialog shows a Weaponised Optimism choice row with Permanent level text, a current value, an arrow to a next value, and an enabled Choose button.

The Stubbornness dialog is rendered with the pickup-value permanent trait at level 0 and below its cap → The pickup-value choice row shows Permanent level 0, a current value of 1, an arrow, a next value of 2 gold per pickup, and an enabled Choose button.

The Stubbornness dialog is rendered with the cost-discount permanent trait at level 1 and below its cap → The cost-discount choice row shows a current value of 5%, an arrow, a next value of 10%, and an enabled Choose button.
The Stubbornness dialog is rendered from saved progress with one unresolved point and three recorded catches → The centered Stubbornness dialog is visible and its ATTEMPTS counter displays 3.

The game completes startup from saved running progress that contains a positive whole-number gold amount and no unresolved Stubbornness choice → The gameplay scene is visible and the GOLD HUD displays the saved whole-number gold amount instead of 0.

Active running play advances for one second with no modal dialog or upgrade panel covering the scene → Clouds, hill bands, and ground decorations translate horizontally across the canvas, and the unicorn cycles vertically above its shadow while the play HUD remains visible.

The unicorn is rendered through one second of active running play → The unicorn changes through at least three distinct gallop poses during the interval and is visible above its shadow throughout the interval.

The leprechaun beside the pot is rendered through one second of active running play → The leprechaun changes through at least two distinct body or leg poses during the interval, and the green shadow beneath it changes width as it hops.

Foliage and the rainbow are rendered through one second of active running play while the rainbow remains in view → Grass, flower, or tree tip pixels shift between adjacent positions during the interval, while the rainbow arc keeps the same band shape and size.

The active gameplay view is rendered while chase approach progress is complete → The unicorn is drawn immediately to the left of the pot of gold with a visible gap between the unicorn sprite and the pot, and both sprites remain on the grass under the rainbow.

The active gameplay HUD is rendered during running play → The GOLD label and number and the Spend Gold button are joined in one centered bottom ribbon, and no separate distance or progress meter is visible in the HUD.
The top-right scene controls are rendered during active running play → The New Game control is shown as a square button in a compact control group pinned near the top-right corner of the scene.

The coin drop timer elapses during running play while the visible coin limit has not been reached → A gold coin appears near the pot of gold and moves away from the pot on a curved path; small gold-colored particles appear around the pot at the same time.

A launched gold coin finishes its landing motion and becomes settled on the grass → The gold coin remains above a small green shadow on the grass and alternates between narrow and wide gold shapes as it bobs.

A gold coin is within the unicorn's magnetic pull range but still outside the collection range during running play → The coin bends toward the unicorn's body and continues moving without an immediate GOLD HUD increase at that moment.

A collectible gold coin reaches the unicorn collection range during running play while the HUD is visible, with no Sparkle upgrade and no permanent pickup-value bonus active → The GOLD HUD number changes from its pre-collection value to that value plus 1 within 0.2 seconds, and a burst of colored sparkle particles appears at the unicorn.

A collectible gold coin reaches the unicorn collection range during running play while the HUD is visible, with exactly one Sparkle upgrade level and no permanent pickup-value bonus active → The GOLD HUD number changes from its pre-collection value to that value plus 2 within 0.2 seconds, and a burst of colored sparkle particles appears at the unicorn.

A collectible gold coin reaches the unicorn collection range during running play while the HUD is visible, with no Sparkle upgrade and exactly one permanent pickup-value bonus active → The GOLD HUD number changes from its pre-collection value to that value plus 2 within 0.2 seconds, and a burst of colored sparkle particles appears at the unicorn.

A collectible gold coin reaches the unicorn collection range during running play while the upgrade panel is open → The upgrade panel stays open, and within 0.2 seconds the panel's displayed GOLD number is different from the value shown immediately before the collection.
A sparkle burst from a collected gold coin is rendered before the burst expires → The burst contains both compact square sparkle particles and thin one-pixel-like streak particles around the unicorn.

Active running play advances for one second while the upgrade panel is open → The upgrade panel remains open in the foreground, and the darkened gameplay scene visible around it continues horizontal scrolling behind the panel.
The upgrade panel header is rendered while the panel is open → The panel header shows a round unicorn portrait, a unicorn name with a short bio, and two stacked stat blocks labeled GOLD and CHASE.

An ordinary upgrade row is rendered in the upgrade panel while that upgrade is below its maximum level → The row shows a current-effect value, an arrow pointing to a next-effect value, a visible Cost label with a gold price, and a purchase button labeled Upgrade.

An ordinary upgrade row is rendered in the upgrade panel while that upgrade is at its maximum level → The row shows ten lit level pips, its Cost label is not visible, and its purchase button displays Maxed.

The upgrade panel is rendered during a fresh run with no permanent discount and Shimmering Mane at level 0 → The Shimmering Mane row is visible with effect text showing Gold drops every, level text indicating 0 of 10, no lit level pips, a cost of 12 gold, and an Upgrade button.

The upgrade panel is rendered during a fresh run with exactly one permanent cost-discount trait active and Shimmering Mane at level 0 → The Shimmering Mane row shows a visible cost of 11 gold and an Upgrade button.

The player activates an affordable ordinary upgrade row below level 9 while the upgrade panel is open during running play → The selected upgrade row refreshes in place: its visible level indicator increases by 1, its displayed next-effect text and Cost label show different text than immediately before activation, and its button remains labeled Upgrade.

The player activates an affordable ordinary upgrade row at level 9 while the upgrade panel is open during running play → The selected upgrade row changes to level 10 of 10 with ten lit pips, its Cost label is not visible, and its purchase button displays Maxed.

The player activates an ordinary upgrade row while the player has insufficient gold for that row → The upgrade panel remains open, and the selected upgrade row keeps the same visible level indicator, effect text, and purchase button state.

The player activates a maxed ordinary upgrade row while the upgrade panel is open during running play → The upgrade panel remains open, and the selected upgrade row continues to show Maxed with the same visible level and effect text.
The Catch the Rainbow row is rendered in the upgrade panel → The row displays the title Catch the Rainbow and a visible cost of 1,000 gold.

The upgrade panel is rendered during running play while at least one ordinary upgrade is not maxed and permanent saving is available → The Catch the Rainbow row shows the button text Locked and the requirement text Max every upgrade to unlock.

The upgrade panel is rendered during running play while every ordinary upgrade is maxed, the catch toll is payable, permanent saving is available, and permanent reward caps have not been reached → The Catch the Rainbow row shows the button text Catch it and the requirement text The rainbow is finally within reach.

The upgrade panel is rendered during running play while every ordinary upgrade is maxed, permanent saving is available, permanent reward caps have not been reached, and the player does not have enough gold for the catch toll → The Catch the Rainbow row shows the requirement text One last treasure toll stands in the way.
