The player activates the Catch the Rainbow control while the catch prerequisites are not satisfied and permanent saving is available → The upgrade panel remains open, the catch control remains in its locked state, and the catch requirement text remains visible.

The player activates the Catch the Rainbow control while the catch is ready, the toll is payable, and saving succeeds → The upgrade list is no longer visible, and the gameplay catch cinematic is visible before the Stubbornness dialog appears.

The upgrade panel is rendered in a narrow viewport at or below the mobile layout breakpoint → The upgrade panel header wraps its stats onto a second row, and each visible upgrade row places its buy controls beneath the upgrade description rather than in a separate right column.

Active gameplay is rendered in a very narrow portrait viewport → The unicorn, the pot of gold, and the leprechaun remain inside the visible canvas area without being cropped off the left or right edge.

The browser viewport is resized during active gameplay → The pixel-art gameplay scene redraws to fill the visible canvas area with no blank gap around the scene, and the HUD controls remain overlaid on the play scene.

games.summaryZh: A colorful turn-based unicorn card game about building a seven-color rainbow before an opponent. Players split revealed unicorn cards into two pairs, choose a pair to keep, use pairs whose values add to seven to create color fragments, discard down to the hand limit, and progress through rounds until a rainbow completion or final scoring decides the match. Interaction is primarily through clicking cards and buttons, dragging cards between areas, and using simple menu and online lobby controls.

requirements.zh: The title screen is displayed → The screen shows the “7 Huenicorns” logo, a “Play” link, a “How to Play?” link, and a Sounds checkbox.
The main page background is rendered → The full page background shows a blue sky gradient above green hill shapes with a repeated paper-texture overlay.

The How to Play screen is displayed → The screen shows the heading “How to Play?”, the text “Build the rainbow before your opponent!”, and five step headings: “1 Split”, “2 Pick”, “3 Make 7”, “4 Make a Fragment”, and “5 Complete the Rainbow”.
The How to Play screen is displayed at the Make 7 step → The Make 7 example shows the combinations “1 + 6”, “2 + 5”, and “3 + 4”, followed by the text “Pair your unicorns whose values add up to 7.”.
The relay online play screen is displayed → The screen shows a “Play” heading, a “Create a game” link, a text input with placeholder “CODE”, and a “Join” link.
A newly created game is first rendered before any player has split cards into pairs → The gameplay area shows the board-game table with a deck area, a pool area, and two pair areas.

The gameplay board is rendered during an active match → A “7 Huenicorns” logo heading is displayed above the board-game table, and the discard-pile button is displayed near the top-right corner of the board.
A round begins with the local human side assigned as the dealer → The status area reads “You are the Dealer: make two pairs”.

During the split phase when the four unicorns have not yet been placed as two cards in Pair A and two cards in Pair B → The action area shows the hint “Drag the four unicorns into two pairs.” and the “Confirm split” button is disabled.

During the split phase when Pair A contains two unicorns and Pair B contains two unicorns → The action area shows the hint “Drag the four unicorns into two pairs.” and the “Confirm split” button is enabled.
During the split phase, a draggable unicorn card is dropped on the Pair A drop area → That unicorn card is displayed inside Pair A, and Pair A’s count reads one higher than before out of 2.
During the split phase, a draggable unicorn card is dropped on the Pair B drop area → That unicorn card is displayed inside Pair B, and Pair B’s count reads one higher than before out of 2.

During the split phase, a draggable unicorn card is dropped on the revealed-cards pool drop area → That unicorn card is displayed in the “✦ Revealed cards ✦” pool, and the pair area it came from shows one fewer card out of 2.

During the split phase, a unicorn from the revealed-cards pool is dropped on Pair A while Pair A already contains two unicorns → The dropped unicorn remains in the “✦ Revealed cards ✦” pool, and Pair A still shows 2 out of 2 cards.
A valid split is confirmed while the local human side is the receiver → The status area reads “You are the Receiver: take one of the two pairs”.
A valid split is confirmed while the opponent side is the receiver → The status area reads “The opponent is choosing…”.
During the choose phase before any pair is selected by the local human side → The action area shows the hint “Pick one pair to keep both its unicorns.” and the “Confirm” button is disabled.

During the choose phase before any pair is selected by the local human side, Pair A is clicked → The action area still shows the hint “Pick one pair to keep both its unicorns.” and the “Confirm” button is enabled.

During the choose phase before any pair is selected by the local human side, Pair B is clicked → The action area still shows the hint “Pick one pair to keep both its unicorns.” and the “Confirm” button is enabled.
The transform phase begins while the local human side is active → The status area reads “Make 7: pair two unicorns that add up to 7, or skip”.
The transform phase begins while the opponent side is active → The status area reads “The opponent is transforming…”.

During the transform phase with no selected unicorn and at least one Make 7 pair available to the local human side → The action area shows the hint “Click a unicorn, then its Make 7 partner, or skip.” and a “Skip” button, and local unicorn cards that can be used in a Make 7 pair are shown with a yellow highlight ring.

During the transform phase with no selected unicorn, a unicorn is clicked → The action hint changes from “Click a unicorn, then its Make 7 partner, or skip.” to “Now click a highlighted partner, or skip.”, and the “Skip” button remains visible.

During the transform phase with one unicorn selected → The selected unicorn card is shown with a yellow outline, valid partner unicorn cards are highlighted, and non-partner local unicorn cards are dimmed.

During the transform phase with no selected unicorn, a local unicorn that is not part of any Make 7 pair is clicked → The action area continues to show “Click a unicorn, then its Make 7 partner, or skip.” with the “Skip” button, and no fragment-choice buttons are shown.

During the transform phase with one unicorn selected, a different local unicorn that does not make 7 with the selected unicorn is clicked → The action area continues to show “Now click a highlighted partner, or skip.” with the “Skip” button, and no fragment-choice buttons are shown.

During the transform phase with one unicorn selected, a partner unicorn is clicked when the two unicorns make 7, have different colors, and both colors are missing from the local human side’s fragments → The action area shows the prompt “Which unicorn becomes a fragment?”, shows two color-choice buttons corresponding to the two selected unicorn colors, and shows a “Cancel” button.

During the transform phase with one unicorn selected, a partner unicorn is clicked when the two unicorns make 7, have different colors, the selected unicorn’s color is missing from the local human side’s fragments, and the clicked partner unicorn’s color is already present in the local human side’s fragments → The selected unicorn card disappears from the local hand and appears in the local fragment row, while the clicked partner unicorn card disappears from the local hand.

During the transform phase with one unicorn selected, a partner unicorn is clicked when the two unicorns make 7, have different colors, the selected unicorn’s color is already present in the local human side’s fragments, and the clicked partner unicorn’s color is missing from the local human side’s fragments → The clicked partner unicorn card disappears from the local hand and appears in the local fragment row, while the selected unicorn card disappears from the local hand.

During the transform phase with one unicorn selected, a partner unicorn is clicked when the two unicorns make 7, have different colors, both colors are already present in the local human side’s fragments, and the shared deck has at least one card → Both selected Make 7 unicorn cards disappear from the local hand, the existing fragments of those colors remain in the local fragment row, and one newly drawn unicorn card appears in the local hand.

During the transform phase with one unicorn selected, a partner unicorn is clicked when the two unicorns make 7, have different colors, both colors are already present in the local human side’s fragments, and the shared deck is empty → Both selected Make 7 unicorn cards disappear from the local hand, the existing fragments of those colors remain in the local fragment row, and no newly drawn unicorn card appears in the local hand.

During the transform phase with one unicorn selected, a partner unicorn is clicked when the two unicorns make 7, have the same color, and that color is missing from the local human side’s fragments → The action area shows a prompt beginning with “You will receive” and ending with “fragment.”, plus an “OK” button and a “Cancel” button.

During the transform phase with one unicorn selected, a partner unicorn is clicked when the two unicorns make 7, have the same color, that color is already present in the local human side’s fragments, and the shared deck has at least one card → Both same-color Make 7 unicorn cards disappear from the local hand, the existing fragment of that color remains in the local fragment row, and one newly drawn unicorn card appears in the local hand.

During the transform phase with one unicorn selected, a partner unicorn is clicked when the two unicorns make 7, have the same color, that color is already present in the local human side’s fragments, and the shared deck is empty → Both same-color Make 7 unicorn cards disappear from the local hand, the existing fragment of that color remains in the local fragment row, and no newly drawn unicorn card appears in the local hand.

During a transform fragment-choice prompt, the “Cancel” button is activated → The action area returns to the hint “Click a unicorn, then its Make 7 partner, or skip.” with a “Skip” button, and the fragment-choice buttons are no longer shown.

A Make 7 transform is confirmed for a color that the acting side does not already have as a fragment → The kept unicorn card disappears from the acting side’s hand and appears in that side’s fragment row, while the discarded partner card disappears from that side’s hand.

A Make 7 transform is confirmed for a color that the acting side already has as a fragment while the shared deck has at least one card → Both Make 7 unicorn cards disappear from the acting side’s hand, the existing fragment of that color remains in the fragment row, and one newly drawn unicorn card appears in the acting side’s hand.

During the transform phase when the local human side is the first transformer of the round, the “Skip” button is activated → The local transform prompt is replaced by the opponent transform state, with the status area reading “The opponent is transforming…”.

During the transform phase when the local human side is the first transformer of the round and has no available Make 7 pair → Within 1 second, the local transform action controls are replaced by the opponent transform state, with the status area reading “The opponent is transforming…”.
After an action, the local human side has too many unicorns and must discard → The status area reads “Too many unicorns — discard down to 5”.
After an action, the opponent side has too many unicorns and must discard → The status area reads “The opponent is discarding…”.
During the discard phase when the local human side has exactly six unicorns → The action area shows the hint “Click 1 unicorn to discard.”.
During the discard phase when the local human side has exactly seven unicorns → The action area shows the hint “Click 2 unicorns to discard.”.

During the discard phase when the local human side has exactly seven unicorns, one of the local unicorn cards is clicked → The clicked unicorn card disappears from the local hand, and the action hint changes to “Click 1 unicorn to discard.”.

During the discard phase when the local human side has exactly six unicorns, one of the local unicorn cards is clicked → The clicked unicorn card disappears from the local hand, and the “Click 1 unicorn to discard.” prompt is no longer shown.
The local player views the game while the opponent is the active side and there is no winner → The action area shows the text “The opponent is playing…”.

An offline game is displaying an opponent-controlled split phase with no winner → Within 1 second, two pair areas contain the four revealed unicorn cards and the status area reads “You are the Receiver: take one of the two pairs” without a player input.

An offline game is displaying an opponent-controlled choose phase with no winner → Within 1 second, the revealed pairs are removed from the center table and the status area reads “The opponent is transforming…” without a player input.
An offline game is displaying an opponent-controlled transform phase with no winner → Within 1 second, the opponent transform state is replaced by a later visible board state without a player input.
An offline game is displaying an opponent-controlled discard phase with no winner → Within 1 second, one opponent hand card is removed from the opponent hand without a player input.
The gameplay board is rendered when both sides have no collected fragments → Each side’s fragment tracker shows seven empty gem icons.

The gameplay board is rendered when the local human side has exactly one collected fragment and the opponent side has no collected fragments → The local human side’s fragment tracker shows one filled gem icon and six empty gem icons, while the opponent side’s fragment tracker shows seven empty gem icons.
The gameplay board is rendered while the discard pile is empty → The discard-pile button reads “Discard: 0”.
The gameplay board is rendered while the discard pile contains exactly one card → The discard-pile button reads “Discard: 1”.
The discard-pile button is activated while the discard pile is empty → An overlay appears with the heading “Discard pile (0)”, the text “The discard pile is empty.”, and a “Close” button.

The discard-pile button is activated while the discard pile contains exactly one card → An overlay appears with the heading “Discard pile (1)”, displays one unicorn card in the discard pile, and shows a “Close” button.
The discard-pile overlay is displayed and its “Close” button is activated → The discard-pile overlay disappears, returning to the gameplay board.

A completed round advances without a winner and the local human side becomes the next dealer → The next round is displayed with the board-game table and the status area reads “You are the Dealer: make two pairs”.
The game reaches a terminal draw state because both sides have at least seven fragments → The board-game table is no longer shown, and the status text reads “It’s a draw!”.
The game ends with both sides having equal fragment counts after final scoring → The board-game table is no longer shown, and the status text reads “It’s a draw!”.
The game reaches a terminal rainbow-completion state with the human side as winner → The board-game table is no longer shown, and the status text reads “You win!”.
The game reaches a terminal rainbow-completion state with the opponent side as winner → The board-game table is no longer shown, and the status text reads “The opponent wins!”.
A final scoring check ends the game with the human side having a higher fragment count than the opponent side → The board-game table is no longer shown, and the status text reads “You win!”.

A final scoring check ends the game with the opponent side having a higher fragment count than the human side → The board-game table is no longer shown, and the status text reads “The opponent wins!”.
A terminal game-over overlay is rendered in an offline game → The overlay shows the final result heading, a “Play again” button, and a “Back to title” button.
A terminal game-over overlay is rendered for an online non-host player → The overlay shows the final result heading, the text “Waiting for the host…”, and a “Back to title” button.

The “Play again” button on a terminal game-over overlay is activated in an offline game → The game-over overlay disappears and a new board-game table is shown with a deck area, a pool area, and two pair areas.
The “Back to title” button on a terminal game-over overlay is activated → The title screen is displayed with the “7 Huenicorns” logo, a “Play” link, and a “How to Play?” link.
An online opponent leaves during a match → An overlay appears with the heading “Opponent left” and a “Back to title” button.

games.summaryZh: A colorful emoji-themed match-3 puzzle game where the player swaps adjacent tiles to create rows or columns of three or more matching symbols. The core loop is selecting tiles with mouse, touch, or keyboard controls, resolving valid swaps into matches, clearing tiles, dropping replacements, scoring points, and continuing through cascades. The game offers Levels mode with move limits and score targets that advance through numbered levels, Time Attack with a countdown and win target, and Endless mode for continuous scoring.

requirements.zh: The game page has completed its initial setup → A control area is visible with three buttons labeled "Levels", "Time Attack", and "Endless".

The player activates the Levels mode button → A fresh Levels game is rendered with a full tile grid and a header displaying "Level: 1", "Score: 0", "Moves: 20", and "Target: 1000"; no game-over overlay text is visible.

The player activates the Time Attack mode button → A fresh Time Attack game is rendered with a full tile grid and a header displaying "Score: 0" and "Time: 60"; the header does not display "Level:", "Moves:", or "Target:", and no game-over overlay text is visible.

The player activates the Endless mode button → A fresh Endless game is rendered with a full tile grid and a header displaying "Score: 0"; the header does not display "Level:", "Moves:", "Time:", or "Target:", and no game-over overlay text is visible.

A fresh playable tile board has been generated for active play → The full grid is visible with no three matching tiles adjacent in an unbroken horizontal row, no three matching tiles adjacent in an unbroken vertical column, and at least one adjacent tile pair whose exchange would create three matching tiles in an unbroken horizontal row or vertical column.
A game frame is rendered during active play → The canvas background is filled with a pastel gradient behind the board.
A playable tile board is rendered during active play → Each occupied grid cell is drawn as a rounded light tile containing a centered emoji symbol.
The player clicks an unselected grid tile during active play → A visible selection outline appears around the clicked tile.
The player taps an unselected grid tile during active play → A visible selection outline appears around the tapped tile.
The player clicks the currently selected grid tile during active play → The selection outline disappears from that tile and no tiles exchange positions.
The player presses Escape while a grid tile is selected during active play → The visible selection outline disappears from the board.

The player clicks a non-adjacent grid tile while another tile is selected during active play → The selection outline moves from the previously selected tile to the clicked tile, and the two tiles do not exchange positions.

The player clicks an adjacent grid tile that is accepted as a move while another tile is selected during active play → The selected tile and the clicked adjacent tile visibly exchange positions on the board.

The player clicks an adjacent grid tile that is rejected as an invalid swap while another tile is selected during active play → The two tiles exchange positions, then return to their original grid cells; after the return, no selection outline is visible.
The player clicks a grid tile while match animations are in progress → The clicked tile does not gain a selection outline and no tile exchange starts from that click.
The player presses ArrowUp during active play while no keyboard cursor is visible → A blue hover outline appears around the tile one row above the board's center tile.

The player presses ArrowUp during active play while the keyboard cursor is visible on a tile that is not in the top row → The blue hover outline moves from its current tile to the tile directly above it.

The player presses ArrowDown during active play while the keyboard cursor is visible on a tile that is not in the bottom row → The blue hover outline moves from its current tile to the tile directly below it.

The player presses ArrowLeft during active play while the keyboard cursor is visible on a tile that is not in the leftmost column → The blue hover outline moves from its current tile to the tile directly to its left.

The player presses ArrowRight during active play while the keyboard cursor is visible on a tile that is not in the rightmost column → The blue hover outline moves from its current tile to the tile directly to its right.
The player clicks outside the tile grid during active play while the keyboard cursor is visible → The blue hover outline disappears from the board.

The player presses ArrowUp while a board tile is selected during active play and the tile directly above is accepted as a move target → The selected tile and the tile directly above it visibly exchange positions on the board.

The player presses ArrowDown while a board tile is selected during active play and the tile directly below is accepted as a move target → The selected tile and the tile directly below it visibly exchange positions on the board.

The player presses ArrowLeft while a board tile is selected during active play and the tile directly to the left is accepted as a move target → The selected tile and the tile directly to the left visibly exchange positions on the board.

The player presses ArrowRight while a board tile is selected during active play and the tile directly to the right is accepted as a move target → The selected tile and the tile directly to the right visibly exchange positions on the board.
The player presses Enter during active play while no grid tile is selected and no keyboard cursor is visible → A visible selection outline appears around the board's center tile.

The player presses Enter during active play while no grid tile is selected and the keyboard cursor is visible on a tile → A visible selection outline appears around the tile that has the blue hover outline.
The player presses Enter during active play while the keyboard cursor is on the currently selected grid tile → The selection outline disappears from that tile and no tiles exchange positions.

The player presses Enter during active play while another tile is selected and the keyboard cursor is on a non-adjacent grid tile → The selection outline moves from the previously selected tile to the keyboard cursor tile, and the two tiles do not exchange positions.

The player presses Enter during active play while another tile is selected and the keyboard cursor is on an adjacent grid tile that is accepted as a move → The selected tile and the keyboard cursor tile visibly exchange positions on the board.

The player presses Enter during active play while another tile is selected and the keyboard cursor is on an adjacent grid tile that is rejected as an invalid swap → The two tiles exchange positions, then return to their original grid cells; after the return, no selection outline is visible.

A match-processing step begins with at least one matched group on the board → The matched tiles shrink out of their grid cells, particle effects appear around the matched area, the header's "Score:" number changes to a new displayed integer, tiles fall vertically into cleared cells, and the board returns to a full grid with no blank cells.

A match-processing step begins with a horizontal matched group on the board → At least three adjacent tiles in one row shrink out of their grid cells, particle effects appear along that row segment, tiles fall vertically into cleared cells, and the board returns to a full grid with no blank cells.

A match-processing step begins with a vertical matched group on the board → At least three adjacent tiles in one column shrink out of their grid cells, particle effects appear along that column segment, tiles fall vertically into cleared cells, and the board returns to a full grid with no blank cells.

A match-processing step begins with a horizontal matched group of at least four adjacent tiles on the board → At least four adjacent tiles in one row shrink out of their grid cells, particle effects appear along that row segment, tiles fall vertically into cleared cells, and the board returns to a full grid with no blank cells.

An apply-gravity animation begins after matched tiles have cleared and at least one replacement tile is spawned above the board → At least one new tile enters from above the top row and moves downward into an empty grid cell; the board ends as a full grid with no blank cells.

A cascade match-processing step begins after falling tiles create another matched group from the same player move → A second set of matched tiles shrinks out and clears without another player selection, and the header's "Score:" number changes again.

A completed valid move leaves the board with no valid moves available → The tile grid is replaced with a full tile grid whose emoji arrangement is not identical to the immediately preceding grid, while the current mode header remains visible.
A valid move in Levels mode is committed while moves remain → The header's "Moves:" number changes from its pre-move value to the next integer down before another player move is accepted.

A resolved move in Levels mode leaves the score at or above the current target score → The level indicator advances to the next level number, the board is redrawn for the new level, and no game-over overlay is visible.
A Levels mode advancement reaches level 2 → The board is replaced with a full new tile grid and the header displays "Level: 2", "Score: 0", "Moves: 19", and "Target: 1500".
A Levels mode advancement reaches level 11 → The board is replaced with a full new tile grid and the header displays "Level: 11", "Score: 0", "Moves: 10", and "Target: 6000".
A Levels mode advancement reaches level 12 → The board is replaced with a full new tile grid and the header displays "Level: 12", "Score: 0", "Moves: 10", and "Target: 6500".
A resolved move in Levels mode leaves zero moves remaining while the score is below the current target score → A game-over overlay appears with the red title text "Out of Moves!".
The player clicks while the Levels loss overlay is showing → The "Out of Moves!" overlay disappears and a fresh Levels game is rendered with "Level: 1" and "Score: 0" in the header.
The player presses Enter while the Levels loss overlay is showing → The "Out of Moves!" overlay disappears and a fresh Levels game is rendered with "Level: 1" and "Score: 0" in the header.

The Time Attack game is active with the header showing a positive "Time:" value greater than 1 and one full second of countdown elapses → The header's "Time:" number changes from its pre-countdown value to the next integer down, and no game-over overlay is displayed.
The Time Attack countdown update reaches zero while the game is not already over → A game-over overlay appears with the red title text "Time's Up!".

A game-over overlay is rendered after a terminal state → A translucent white panel covers the gameplay view, with a centered title line above a centered "Score:" line and the instruction text "Press Enter or click to play again" below it.
The player clicks while the Time Attack loss overlay is showing → The "Time's Up!" overlay disappears and a new Time Attack board is rendered.

games.summaryZh: Unicorn Storm is a rhythm memory game themed around a herd of colorful unicorns. The player watches unicorns perform a growing musical pattern, then repeats it by tapping herd columns or pressing number keys with accurate timing. Runs progress by passing rounds to add notes, with score, best records, timing feedback, midair bonus effects, retries, and a harder height-matching mode. The game also includes song selection, free jam recording, custom pattern creation, share links, and playful storm, rainbow, and unicorn animation feedback.

requirements.zh: The normal unshared title screen is rendered after initial setup with no run starting → The title screen shows "UNICORN STORM" near the upper center, the subtitle "Simon says repeat after the unicorns" directly below it, the text "turn on yer sound" near the bottom, buttons labeled "SONGS", "JAM", and "PATTERN", and a decorative "HARDCORE" button.

A gameplay frame is rendered while the game is paused because the audio context is not running → A dark translucent overlay covers the playfield with the centered text "paused" and the instruction "tap anywhere to resume" below it.
The player taps the screen while the paused overlay is visible and audio can resume → The "paused" and "tap anywhere to resume" overlay is no longer visible, revealing the gameplay screen underneath.

A gameplay frame is rendered while a mid-pattern restart prompt is active → A dark overlay shows the text "start this pattern over" near the upper center with "your score and streak carry on" directly below it.
A gameplay frame is rendered with persistent controls while beat visualization is enabled → Three labeled controls are visible: "RESTART", "BEAT ON", and "HOME".
The player activates the beat toggle while its visible label reads "BEAT ON" → The beat toggle's visible label changes to "BEAT OFF".
The player activates the beat toggle while its visible label reads "BEAT OFF" → The beat toggle's visible label changes to "BEAT ON".
The player activates the home control during a non-title gameplay screen → The display returns to the title screen with "UNICORN STORM" near the upper center.
The player activates the restart control during an in-progress pattern → A dark overlay appears with the text "start this pattern over" and the line "your score and streak carry on" below it.
The player presses keyboard key 1 during a phase that accepts herd note input → The leftmost unicorn performs a visible note-response animation from the herd row.

The player gives a quick pointer tap on the leftmost unicorn's herd column during a phase that accepts herd note input → The leftmost unicorn performs a visible note-response animation from the herd row.

The player gives a quick pointer tap on the second unicorn's herd column during a phase that accepts herd note input → The second unicorn from the left performs a visible note-response animation from the herd row.
The player gives a quick pointer tap on the center unicorn's herd column during a phase that accepts herd note input → The center unicorn performs a visible note-response animation from the herd row.

The player gives a quick pointer tap on the fourth unicorn's herd column during a phase that accepts herd note input → The second unicorn from the right performs a visible note-response animation from the herd row.

The player gives a quick pointer tap on the rightmost unicorn's herd column during a phase that accepts herd note input → The rightmost unicorn performs a visible note-response animation from the herd row.

The player drags from one herd column into a different herd column during a phase that accepts slide input → The newly entered unicorn column performs its own visible note-response animation after the previous column's animation.
The player presses and holds a numbered keyboard key while the game page has not yet shown keyboard controls → Small keycap boxes appear below the five unicorns on the ground row.

The title screen is rendered after loading a valid shared pattern link with a shared name → The title screen shows a line beginning with "someone sent you" and containing the shared name, and the normal decorative "HARDCORE" button is replaced by a button labeled "NEW GAME".
The player activates the "SONGS" menu button on the title screen → The screen changes to a song-pick menu with the heading "songs" and the subtitle "real tunes, revealed a note at a time".
A song-pick menu frame is rendered with the built-in song list → At least three song choice rows are visible, and each row shows a song title with a subtitle ending in "notes".
The player activates a song choice row on the song-pick menu → A run begins and the gameplay screen shows a countdown message beginning with "the unicorns play in".
The player activates the back control on the song-pick menu → The display returns to the title screen with "UNICORN STORM" near the upper center.

The player activates the normal unshared "HARDCORE" title button → A hardcore briefing screen appears with the heading "HARDCORE", the text "TAP for a low hop", "HOLD for a high leap", and "match the jump height", and buttons labeled "BRING IT ON" and "BACK".
The player activates the "BACK" control on the hardcore briefing screen → The display returns to the title screen with "UNICORN STORM" near the upper center.
The player activates the "BRING IT ON" control on the hardcore briefing screen → A run begins and the gameplay screen shows a countdown message beginning with "the unicorns play in".
The player starts a normal run from the title screen → A run begins and the gameplay screen shows a countdown message beginning with "the unicorns play in".
The player activates the "JAM" menu button on the title screen → The screen changes to jam mode with visible controls labeled "BACK", a beat toggle, and "REC".
The player activates the jam "BACK" control → The display returns to the title screen with "UNICORN STORM" near the upper center.
The player activates the jam record control while recording is inactive → The jam record control changes to "STOP" and the text "recording — 0 notes" is displayed.
The player activates the jam stop control after recording fewer than two notes → The jam record control changes back to "REC" and no share-link input is visible.
The player activates the jam stop control after recording at least two notes → A share panel opens with a visible share-link input containing a URL.
A shared jam replay frame is rendered for a shared jam with a name → The screen shows the shared jam name and the normal score HUD line is not displayed.
A shared jam replay reaches its end → The display returns to the title screen with "UNICORN STORM" near the upper center.

The player activates the "PATTERN" menu button on the title screen → The screen changes to pattern-composition mode with the heading "make a pattern" and controls including "NORMAL", "HEAR", "CLEAR", "DONE", and "BACK".
A pattern-composition frame is rendered while the composed pattern is empty → The "HEAR", "CLEAR", and "DONE" controls are visible in a locked gray style.
The player activates the "NORMAL" control in pattern-composition mode → The same control changes from "NORMAL" to rainbow "HARDCORE" lettering.
The player activates the decorative hardcore control in pattern-composition mode → The same control changes back to the label "NORMAL".
The player enters the first note in an empty pattern-composition sequence → A visible pattern timeline appears with one colored note marker.

A pattern-composition frame is rendered while the composed pattern contains exactly one note → The "HEAR" and "CLEAR" controls are visible in their enabled style, while the "DONE" control remains in a locked gray style.

The player enters a note while the pattern-composition timeline contains exactly one note → The visible pattern timeline contains two colored note markers and the "DONE" control is shown as the gold action button.
The player activates "DONE" in pattern-composition mode while the pattern contains at least two notes → A share panel opens with a visible share-link input containing a URL.
The player activates "CLEAR" in pattern-composition mode after at least one note has been added → The pattern timeline note markers disappear and the screen remains on the "make a pattern" composer.
The player activates "BACK" in pattern-composition mode → The display returns to the title screen with "UNICORN STORM" near the upper center.
The player activates "HEAR" in pattern-composition mode after at least one note has been added → The composed notes play back visibly as unicorn note-response animations in the pattern order.
A share panel frame is rendered for a recorded jam → The panel shows the heading "share your jam!!", the instruction "tap the link, then long-press to copy", an "OK" button, and the share-link input.

A share panel frame is rendered for a composed pattern → The panel shows the heading "share your pattern!!", the instruction "tap the link, then long-press to copy", an "OK" button, and the share-link input.
A share panel frame is rendered with the share-link input visible → A second text input is visible for naming the share, showing the placeholder text "name it (optional)" when it is empty.

The player types into the name input while the share panel is open and the share-link input is visible → The typed name appears in the name input, and the visible URL text in the share-link input updates.

A countdown frame is rendered during a play-in or turn-handoff countdown → A large countdown numeral is shown below the countdown label, with a thin white circular timing ring drawn around the numeral area.
A call phase frame is rendered after the initial play-in countdown and before the response handoff countdown → The text "watch the unicorns" appears near the upper part of the playfield.
The call phase reaches a pattern note for a unicorn → That unicorn performs a visible note-response leap and the corresponding progress marker changes from a dim marker to that unicorn's color.
The call phase reaches a high-note slot in a height-enabled pattern → The calling unicorn performs a high soar with visible wings.
The run transitions from the unicorn call phase into the player's response phase → A large "GO" text appears near the upper part of the playfield.

A response phase frame is rendered after the "GO" text has faded and before the player has entered the first response note → The text "your turn" is shown near the upper part of the playfield with "the beat starts on your first note" directly below it.

A normal gameplay frame is rendered while the score HUD is available → A bottom HUD line is visible in the format "N pts · best M", with a current score number followed by "pts" and a best score number after "best".
A gameplay pattern with 16 or fewer notes is displayed → The progress display uses individual note dots laid out across the top of the playfield.
A gameplay pattern with more than 16 notes is displayed → The progress display uses a compact bar instead of individual note dots across the top of the playfield.

The player enters the correct first note of a pattern during the first accepted input slot while the bottom score HUD reads "0 pts" and the current score multiplier is x1 → A floating green "go!" label appears at the activated unicorn, and the bottom score HUD updates to begin with "100 pts".
The player enters a note that is not the correct first note of a pattern during the first accepted input slot → A floating red "wrong one" label appears at the activated unicorn.

The player enters a correct later pattern note with the PERFECT timing tier while the current score multiplier is x1 → A floating "PERFECT" label appears at the activated unicorn, and the bottom score HUD current-score number increases by 100 points from its pre-input displayed value.

The player enters a correct later pattern note with the GOOD timing tier while the current score multiplier is x1 → A floating "GOOD" label appears at the activated unicorn, and the bottom score HUD current-score number increases by 60 points from its pre-input displayed value.

The player enters a correct later pattern note inside the timing window with an unnamed early timing tier while the current score multiplier is x1 → A floating label appears at the activated unicorn beginning with "early " and ending with "ms", and the bottom score HUD current-score number increases by 30 points from its pre-input displayed value.

The player enters a correct later pattern note inside the timing window with an unnamed late timing tier while the current score multiplier is x1 → A floating label appears at the activated unicorn beginning with "late " and ending with "ms", and the bottom score HUD current-score number increases by 30 points from its pre-input displayed value.

The player enters the wrong unicorn for a later pattern note inside its timing window while the score HUD is visible → A floating red "wrong one" label appears at the activated unicorn, and the bottom score HUD current-score number remains unchanged during the following half second.

The player enters an extra note during response when no unjudged pattern slot is inside the timing window while the score HUD is visible → A floating "extra" label appears at the activated unicorn, and the bottom score HUD current-score number remains unchanged during the following half second.

The response window ends while one or more pattern notes have not been played → A red "missed" label appears above each unicorn whose expected note was not played, and the round advances to the result overlay.
The player keeps holding a launched note until the high-jump threshold in a height-enabled response → The flying unicorn switches into a high soar with visible wings and a white glow around it.
The player releases a held note before the high-jump threshold in a height-enabled response → The launched unicorn continues as a low hop without wings appearing.

A live metronome beat begins while beat visualization is enabled during a phase where the beat pulse is active → The ground band below the herd changes from its pre-beat dark blue state to a blue flash, and the thin cyan line along the top of the ground band changes to a vivid cyan line; both return to the pre-beat state within one third of a beat.
A scheduled unicorn leap effect reaches its scheduled display time → A flying unicorn copy appears from the herd row at the scheduled unicorn position and begins moving through the playfield.
A flying unicorn copy reaches the left playfield wall → The copy remains inside the playfield and reverses from leftward motion to rightward motion.
A flying unicorn copy reaches the top playfield boundary → The copy remains inside the playfield and reverses from upward motion to downward motion.
A flying unicorn copy falls below the bottom of the playfield → The copy is no longer visible in the playfield.

Two bonus-eligible unicorn leap effects intersect in midair while the current score multiplier is x1 → A burst effect appears at the intersection point and a yellow floating "+250" score popup appears there.

Two bonus-eligible unicorn leap effects intersect in midair while the current score multiplier is x5 → A burst effect appears at the intersection point and a yellow floating "+1250" score popup appears there.
Two unicorn leap effects intersect in midair while at least one is not bonus-eligible → A burst effect appears at the intersection point.
A round celebration is triggered with accuracy at least 0.95 → The screen shows a blue-white flash, three rainbow arcs, and fireworks effects.
A round celebration is triggered with accuracy at least 0.9 and below 0.95 → Two rainbow arcs appear behind the playfield and at least four unicorn leap effects occur during the celebration.
A round celebration is triggered with accuracy at least 0.8 and below 0.9 → Three unicorn leap effects occur in sequence during the celebration, and no rainbow arc appears from this celebration.
A round celebration is triggered with accuracy at least 0.5 and below 0.8 → One center-unicorn leap effect occurs during the celebration, and no rainbow arc appears from this celebration.
A round is evaluated with accuracy greater than 0.98 → The round result message "PERFECT" is displayed.
A round is evaluated with accuracy at least 0.5 and at most 0.98 when the round message selector chooses the first pass message → The round result message "nice" is displayed.
A round is evaluated with accuracy below 0.5 when the round message selector chooses the first fail message → The round result message "not quite" is displayed.

A completed round result overlay is rendered with no mid-pattern restart → The overlay shows the round message near the upper center with a line directly below it formatted as an integer followed by "% match", and choices labeled "TRY AGAIN" and "HEAR IT AGAIN" are visible.
A round result overlay is shown after at least one midair bonus collision occurred during the round → A line ending in "midair bonus" appears below the match percentage on the result overlay.

A round result overlay is shown after a mid-pattern restart → The result choices include "TRY AGAIN" with "same pattern, play now", "HEAR IT AGAIN" with "the unicorns play it first", and a locked "NEXT!" choice with "finish the pattern first".
A round result overlay is shown after a completed round with accuracy at least 0.5 and no mid-pattern restart → The result choices include "NEXT!" with the subtitle "one note longer".
A round result overlay is shown after a completed round with accuracy below 0.5 → The result choices include a locked "NEXT!" choice with the subtitle "needs 50%".
The player activates "NEXT!" on an eligible non-restart passing result overlay → A new round begins and the gameplay screen shows a countdown message beginning with "the unicorns play in".

The player activates "HEAR IT AGAIN" on a result overlay after the input guard interval has passed → The same pattern begins again with the unicorn call countdown beginning with "the unicorns play in".

The player activates an enabled "TRY AGAIN" choice on a result overlay after the input guard interval has passed → The result overlay disappears, the gameplay response screen appears, and a large "GO" text is visible near the upper part of the playfield without a "the unicorns play in" countdown.
A round is evaluated with a current score greater than the previously displayed best score → The bottom score HUD shows the best score number updated to match the current score number.

A new passing round begins after a completed round whose visible progress display used 15 or fewer individual note dots → The new round's progress display uses individual note dots and contains exactly one additional note dot compared with the previous completed round's progress display.
A weather lightning timer elapses during a rendered frame → A forked lightning bolt appears in the sky and a pale flash overlays the scene.

games.summaryZh: A canvas-based sorting and cleanup game with a playful animal-stable theme. The player arranges colored cards by dragging them into an accepted order, activates a progression button to advance through animated reward/progress sequences, watches fruits collect and disappear, then switches to a broom interaction to clean poop targets. Completing the cleanup leads to a thank-you end scene with a walking horse animation, fade-out, and automatic reset back to the starting sorting loop.

requirements.zh: The initial game scene has completed setup → The playfield is visible on a black background with a horizontal row of colored cards, fruit sprites, and a progression button.
A card is held after being pressed during the interactive sorting phase → The selected card is drawn above the other cards in the row, and its horizontal position follows the cursor while it is held.
A dragged card becomes closer to a different slot than to its current target slot → The non-dragged card occupying that slot slides horizontally toward the slot that the dragged card left.
The pointer is released while a dragged card is offset from its assigned slot → The released card stops following the cursor and slides horizontally toward its assigned slot in the card row.
The current visible card arrangement has three distinct colors in the required color order during the interactive sorting phase → The progression button is drawn at full opacity.
The current visible card arrangement contains fewer than three distinct colors during the interactive sorting phase → The progression button is drawn at full opacity.

The current visible card arrangement has three distinct colors in an order that is not the required color order during the interactive sorting phase → The progression button is drawn translucent at 13% opacity.

The hovered progression button is activated while the current visible card arrangement has three distinct colors in the required color order → The progression sequence starts: the progression button is drawn translucent during its click flicker, and large progress sprites begin appearing in the play area.

The hovered progression button is activated while the visible cards contain fewer than three distinct colors → The progression sequence starts: the progression button is drawn translucent during its click flicker, and large progress sprites begin appearing in the play area.

The hovered progression button is activated while the current visible card arrangement has three distinct colors in an order that is not the required color order → The progression button is drawn at alternating horizontal offsets while the cards remain in the same left-to-right slot order.
The level progress indicator is below its target during active play → The progression button moves horizontally to the right between consecutive rendered frames.

The successful progression animation reaches the display threshold for the second large progress sprite before the final flash interval → A second large tilted progress sprite is drawn in the play area while the first large progress sprite remains visible.
The successful progression animation enters its final flash interval → The displayed large progress sprites alternate between full opacity and 30% opacity for 1 second.
A visible uncollected fruit is in its normal active-play bobbing state → That fruit remains visible and its drawn vertical position cycles upward and downward over consecutive rendered frames.

An uncollected fruit reaches the collection line at the progression button during active play → That fruit begins its collection animation by being drawn higher over consecutive frames instead of continuing its normal up-and-down bobbing cycle.
A collected fruit has finished its collection and flashing intervals during active play → That fruit is no longer drawn in the play area.

The last fruit has disappeared while the game is still in the sorting phase → The card row is no longer drawn, eight poop cleanup targets appear in the play area, and the cursor is represented by a broom sprite.

A broom stroke is applied to a poop target showing its initial dirty appearance while the cleanup cooldown is ready → That poop target changes to its next cleaned appearance, and the broom sprite flips to the opposite sweep pose.

A broom stroke is applied to a poop target showing its second cleaned appearance while the cleanup cooldown is ready → That poop target is no longer drawn as a cleanup target, and the broom sprite flips to the opposite sweep pose.

A broom stroke is attempted on a poop target while that poop target's cleanup cooldown has not expired → That poop target keeps the same dirty or cleaned appearance on the next rendered frame after the attempted stroke.

All poop cleanup targets have been removed and the thank-you delay has expired → The cleanup play scene is no longer visible, and the thank-you end scene with a horse sprite and patterned rain sheets is drawn.

The thank-you end scene horse animation advances from its first walking frame to its second walking frame → The horse sprite changes from the first walking pose to the second walking pose while the thank-you scene remains visible.
The thank-you end scene begins its fade-out phase → A dark overlay covers the thank-you scene, and by the end of the fade the rendered view is fully black.
The post-fade black screen timer finishes after the thank-you scene → The game resets to the initial sorting scene with cards, fruits, and the progression button visible again.

games.summaryZh: An isometric 3D puzzle-adventure about navigating log-like levels in a web-themed story. The player guides a main character across grid tiles, manipulates draggable blocks, uses teleporters, avoids moving eye enemies, and reaches exit teleporters to progress through built-in levels. The game begins from a mock download/landing page, presents story dialogue between levels, supports subscriber custom-level loading, and ends through download-style success or error flows.

requirements.zh: The game starts for a first-time visitor before the initial help has been dismissed → A modal help window is visible over the directory-style page, with a close button marked "×" and the heading "Welcome to An HTTP Story".
A visible modal window close control is clicked while a modal window is open → The open modal window and dark modal overlay disappear, leaving the directory-style main page visible.
The help control is clicked while the main page is visible → The modal overlay opens with the help window visible
The monetization/custom-level control is clicked while the main page is visible → The modal overlay opens with the monetization/custom-level window visible
The start/download control is clicked while the main page is visible → The download bar is visible and its message reads "Preparing download..."

The initial start/download flow reaches the first 2-second wait after showing the download message "Preparing download..." → The download bar remains visible and its message changes to "Unexpected error"
The initial download preparation completes after the start/download flow → The landing page is hidden, the gameplay canvas is visible, and the bottom download bar is no longer open over the page
Built-in level 1 is loaded into the gameplay scene → The isometric 3D level view is shown and a dialogue overlay displays the line "Ouch... Where am I?"
Built-in level 2 is loaded into the gameplay scene → The isometric 3D level view is shown and a dialogue overlay displays the line "Damn. Still the wrong address."
Built-in level 3 is loaded into the gameplay scene → The isometric 3D level view is shown and a dialogue overlay displays the line "Process 15127:"
Built-in level 4 is loaded into the gameplay scene → The isometric 3D level view is shown and a dialogue overlay displays the line "Process 15127:"
Built-in level 5 is loaded into the gameplay scene → The isometric 3D level view is shown and a dialogue overlay displays the line "You don't say much, do you?"
Built-in level 6 is loaded into the gameplay scene → The isometric 3D level view is shown and a dialogue overlay displays the line "We're getting close. I can feel it."
Built-in level 7 is loaded into the gameplay scene → The isometric 3D level view is shown and a dialogue overlay displays the line "Anomaly detected. Beginning quarantine."
Built-in level 8 is loaded into the gameplay scene → The isometric 3D level view is shown and a dialogue overlay displays the line "Whew... That was too close!"

A dialogue sequence has another queued line when the currently displayed line's wait completes → The currently displayed dialogue text is replaced by the next dialogue line in the same dialogue overlay
A dialogue sequence reaches the end when the final displayed line's wait completes → The dialogue text is erased and the dialogue background panel is no longer visible
A level-completion event occurs on a level that has outro dialogue lines → The current level remains visible and a dialogue overlay displays an outro line before the level changes
The main character is instructed to walk to the grid tile it already occupies during active gameplay → The main character remains on its current grid tile and no walking path animation begins

The main character is instructed to walk toward a reachable tile whose next step is along the x-axis during active gameplay → The main character leaves its current tile and moves one grid tile along the x-axis toward the selected destination

The main character is instructed to walk toward a reachable tile whose next step is along the z-axis during active gameplay → The main character leaves its current tile and moves one grid tile along the z-axis toward the selected destination

The main character is instructed to walk toward a reachable destination that differs on both the x-axis and z-axis while the next x-axis and z-axis tiles are both walkable → The main character moves one grid tile along the x-axis and then one grid tile along the z-axis toward the selected destination without another instruction

The main character is instructed to walk toward a same-row destination while the adjacent x-axis tile in that direction is not walkable → The main character does not enter the blocked adjacent x-axis tile in response to the instruction
A hoverable 3D object is pointed at during active gameplay while no drag is starting → A white overlay highlight appears on the pointed object
The pointer leaves a highlighted non-dragged 3D object during active gameplay → The white overlay highlight is removed from that object
A draggable block has been held for the drag-start delay during active gameplay while the main character is not standing on it → An outline appears around the selected block

A draggable block is picked for dragging while the main character is standing on top of it → An outline appears on the block, and the block stays at its original grid position while the main character remains on top of it
A draggable object is dragged during active gameplay → The dragged 3D object moves from its starting tile position while the rest of the level remains in place
A dragged block overlaps another solid object during active gameplay → The dragged block remains outlined while overlapping the other object
A dragged block is released while its nearest snapped grid tile is safe → The block glides from its released position to the nearest grid-aligned tile and comes to rest there

A dragged block is released while its nearest snapped grid tile is unsafe, its x-axis offset from that nearest tile is greater than its z-axis offset, and the x-axis fallback tile is safe → The block glides to the grid-aligned tile adjacent to the nearest snapped tile along the x-axis and comes to rest there
A dragged block is released while no safe snapped grid position is available → The block glides back to the grid tile where the drag began and comes to rest there
The main character enters a paired non-exit teleporter during active gameplay → The main character disappears at the entered teleporter and reappears at the matching teleporter elsewhere in the level

The main character enters the special exit teleporter on a built-in level that has a following built-in level → The current level scene clears and the next built-in level appears with its dialogue overlay

The main character enters the special exit teleporter on the final built-in level → The current level scene clears and the page returns to the ending download flow, with the download bar opening over the page
A seeker eye enemy is present in a loaded level → The eye enemy is visible with red surfaces and one white face
A non-seeker eye enemy is present in a loaded level → The eye enemy is visible with a red face
A patrolling eye enemy has a defined patrol path when the level becomes ready → The eye enemy begins moving between patrol waypoints in the level

A seeker enemy update occurs while player control is active and the main character is at a different grid position from the seeker → The seeker eye rotates so its visible face points toward the main character during the update

A seeker enemy update occurs while the main character is offset only along the x-axis and the adjacent x-axis tile is not already targeted by another seeker → The seeker enemy moves one grid tile along the x-axis from its current tile toward the main character

A seeker enemy update occurs while the main character is offset only along the z-axis and the adjacent z-axis tile is not already targeted by another seeker → The seeker enemy moves one grid tile along the z-axis from its current tile toward the main character

A seeker enemy update occurs while the main character is offset from the seeker along both the x-axis and z-axis and neither adjacent target tile is already targeted by another seeker → The seeker enemy moves from its current tile to a diagonally adjacent tile, changing by one grid tile along the x-axis and one grid tile along the z-axis during the update

An enemy eye touches the main character while player control is active → The eye enemy surrounds the main character, and the main character disappears from the level view during the capture animation.
The ending download sequence begins after gameplay reaches an ending state → A modal overlay is visible, the download bar opens, and the download bar message reads "Preparing download..."
The losing ending download preparation completes → The download bar message reads "Unexpected error" and the unexpected-error notification is visible
The winning ending download preparation completes → The download bar message reads "Click to open" and a download item row is visible

The visible unexpected-error download notification is clicked after the losing ending is prepared → The unexpected-error notification is no longer visible, and a window is visible with the heading "This server has been confiscated by the Ministry of Knowledge."
The clickable download item is clicked after the winning ending is prepared → A window is visible with a 👾 icon and the heading "Thanks for playing An HTTP Story!"

The custom-level import/create screen is shown for a Coil subscriber → A window is visible with the heading "Thanks for being a Coil subscriber!", instructions beginning "Load a custom level from", a text area containing JSON level data, and a "Play" button
Web monetization starts while the monetization/custom-level page elements are available → The non-subscriber monetization elements are hidden and the subscriber custom-level elements are visible
The custom-level form is submitted with valid custom level data in the text area → The custom level opens in the isometric 3D level view
The custom-level form is submitted with invalid custom level data in the text area → The custom-level window remains visible with its text area and Play button, and no isometric level scene opens

games.summaryZh: Rainbow Run is a colorful endless runner about guiding a unicorn along a rainbow road, collecting crystals and power-up drops while avoiding lane obstacles and road-edge falls. The player uses lane changes, jumps, slides, and menu controls to survive, gather crystals, and extend each run. Runs end on a results screen, earned crystals support upgrades, and best distance progression is reflected back on the title screen.

requirements.zh: The initial game page has completed setup on the title screen → The UI shows the rainbow title text "RAINBOW RUN", a best-distance plate ending in "m", a "CRYSTALS" plate, and menu buttons labeled "START", "UPGRADES", and either "SOUND: ON" or "SOUND: OFF".

The START button is activated on the title screen → The title menu is replaced by the running gameplay view; the title text and title menu buttons are absent, and a pause control is visible over the gameplay.

The UPGRADES button is activated on the title screen → The screen changes to an upgrades menu showing the heading "UPGRADES", a "CRYSTALS" plate, and upgrade option buttons with rank text containing a number, "/", and each upgrade cap.

A new active run begins after the player state is reset → The gameplay HUD shows a distance plate ending in "m" near the top center, a crystal-count plate near the top-right edge, and a lives display containing 2 life markers.
The active running gameplay UI is rendered → A dark rounded pause button appears near the upper-left corner with two white vertical bars inside it.

Active running gameplay advances far enough for the displayed distance counter to reach its next meter value → The distance plate near the top center changes from its immediately previous number to a new number ending in "m".
The pause control is activated during active running gameplay → A translucent dark overlay covers the gameplay, the text "PAUSED" appears, and menu buttons labeled "RESUME" and "QUIT" are visible.
The game is paused and the RESUME button is activated → The pause overlay, "PAUSED" text, and pause menu buttons disappear, returning to the running gameplay view with the pause control visible.

The game is paused and the QUIT button is activated → The game leaves the paused run and returns to the title screen with the "RAINBOW RUN" title and the "START", "UPGRADES", and sound menu buttons visible.

The BACK button is activated from the upgrades menu → The upgrades heading and upgrade buttons disappear, and the title screen returns with the "RAINBOW RUN" title and the "START", "UPGRADES", and sound menu buttons visible.

A completed run reaches the death screen with recorded distance and collected-crystal values → A translucent dark overlay covers the gameplay, the death overlay shows the rainbow heading "RUN OVER", a distance value ending in "m", a line beginning with "+" and ending with "CRYSTALS", and the prompt "TAP TO CONTINUE" near the bottom of the screen.

The death screen is displayed and the player taps or clicks → The death overlay disappears and the title screen returns with the "RAINBOW RUN" title and the "START", "UPGRADES", and sound menu buttons visible.

The ArrowLeft lane command is processed during active running gameplay while the adjacent screen-left lane is available → The runner leaves the current lane and moves toward the adjacent lane on the screen-left side of the track.

The ArrowRight lane command is processed during active running gameplay while the adjacent screen-right lane is available → The runner leaves the current lane and moves toward the adjacent lane on the screen-right side of the track.
The ArrowUp jump command is processed during active running gameplay while jumping is available → The runner rises above the running surface while continuing forward along the track.
The ArrowDown slide command is processed during active running gameplay while sliding is available → The runner lowers into a sliding posture on the track while continuing forward.

A jump command is processed during active running gameplay while the runner is sliding and slide cancellation is available → The runner leaves the lowered sliding posture and returns to an upright running posture without rising above the running surface.

A jump command is processed during active running gameplay while the runner is sliding and slide cancellation is unavailable → The runner remains in the lowered sliding posture and does not rise above the running surface within the next 0.5 seconds.

A slide command is processed during active running gameplay while the runner is airborne and jump cancellation is available → Within the next 0.5 seconds, the runner descends toward the running surface and does not remain on its immediately previous upward jump arc.

A slide command is processed during active running gameplay while the runner is airborne and jump cancellation is unavailable → The runner remains airborne on its current arc and does not enter the lowered sliding posture within the next 0.5 seconds.

A screen-left lane-change command is processed during active running gameplay while the runner is already in the outer screen-left lane, charge is inactive, and invincibility is inactive → Within 1 second, the runner moves sideways off the screen-left road edge, the lives display contains exactly 1 fewer life marker than it contained immediately before the command, and the running gameplay remains visible if at least 1 life marker remains.

A screen-left lane-change command is processed during active running gameplay while the runner is already in the outer screen-left lane and charge is active → The runner remains on the road in the screen-left outer lane, the charge meter remains visible, and the lives display contains the same number of life markers as immediately before the command.

A screen-left lane-change command is processed during active running gameplay while the runner is already in the outer screen-left lane, charge is inactive, and invincibility is active → The runner remains on the road in the screen-left outer lane, and the lives display contains the same number of life markers as immediately before the command.

The player takes a hit during active running gameplay while exactly 1 life marker is shown and invincibility is not active → The lives display reaches 0 life markers and the run transitions into the death-screen overlay with the "TAP TO CONTINUE" prompt.

The active running gameplay is in an invincibility-frames state while the runner is not falling, swooping, or dying → During the invincibility interval, the unicorn alternates between rendered frames where it is visible and rendered frames where it is hidden, while the road and HUD remain visible.

The runner collects a crystal at a visible pickup position during active running gameplay → The crystal is no longer visible at the pickup position, and the crystal-count plate near the top-right edge shows a number exactly 1 higher than it showed immediately before the pickup.

A crystal is within magnet attraction range during active running gameplay while the runner is on the track and the crystal is outside the immediate pickup radius → Across the next 0.5 seconds, the crystal leaves its prior path position and moves toward the runner before it is collected or passes out of view.
A shield drop is present ahead during active running gameplay → A golden spinning octahedron-shaped pickup is visible above the road.
The runner collects a shield drop during active running gameplay → The collected drop disappears, and a translucent golden shield bubble appears around the unicorn.

The runner takes a non-falling hit during active running gameplay while the shield bubble is visible and invincibility is inactive → Within the next rendered frame, the shield bubble is no longer visible and the lives display contains the same number of life markers as immediately before the hit.
The runner collects a wings drop during active running gameplay → The collected drop disappears, and a pair of wings becomes visible on the unicorn.

The runner takes a falling hit during active running gameplay while wings are visible and invincibility is inactive → Within 1 second, the unicorn performs a swooping recovery motion back toward the road, the wings remain visible during the recovery, and the lives display contains the same number of life markers as immediately before the hit.
The runner collects a charge drop during active running gameplay → The collected drop disappears, and a horizontal charge meter appears below the lives display.

An active charge overlaps an obstacle in the runner's lane during active running gameplay → The obstacle breaks into visible fragments and is removed from the road, while the lives display contains the same number of life markers as immediately before the overlap.
The active charge meter depletes during active running gameplay → The horizontal charge meter below the lives display disappears.

The runner reaches a crystal during active charge while the crystal is inside the charge pickup range → The crystal disappears from the track, and the crystal-count plate near the top-right edge increases by 1 compared with immediately before the pickup.

The runner collects a heart drop during active running gameplay while the current lives count is below the maximum lives count → The collected drop disappears, and within the next rendered frame the lives display contains exactly 1 additional life marker compared with immediately before collection.

The runner overlaps a blocking obstacle during active running gameplay while charge is inactive, invincibility is inactive, the runner is on the track, and no pass-through state is active → The obstacle breaks into visible fragments, and within the next rendered frame the lives display contains exactly 1 fewer life marker than it contained immediately before the overlap.

The runner reaches a high obstacle in the same lane during active running gameplay while sliding low enough to pass under it → The runner passes under the high obstacle with no obstacle fragments appearing, and the lives display contains the same number of life markers as immediately before reaching the obstacle.

The runner reaches a low obstacle in the same lane during active running gameplay while airborne high enough to pass over it → The runner passes over the low obstacle with no obstacle fragments appearing, and the lives display contains the same number of life markers as immediately before reaching the obstacle.
The runner overlaps an obstacle during active running gameplay while invincibility is active → The lives display contains the same number of life markers as immediately before the overlap.

An affordable, not-maxed upgrade option is activated from the upgrades menu → The selected upgrade option's displayed rank changes from N/C to (N+1)/C, and the crystals total shown on the upgrades menu changes from its previous number to that previous number minus the price number that was shown on the selected upgrade option immediately before activation.

An unaffordable, not-maxed upgrade option is activated from the upgrades menu → The upgrades menu remains visible, the selected upgrade option's displayed rank is unchanged from immediately before activation, and the crystals total is unchanged from immediately before activation.

A completed run reaches the death screen after recording a new best distance → The death overlay includes the text "NEW BEST!" in addition to the run-over information and the "TAP TO CONTINUE" prompt.
The title screen is shown after a completed run recorded a new best distance → The best-distance plate displays the completed run's distance in meters instead of the previous best value.

The upgrades menu is displaying a not-maxed upgrade row → That upgrade row label includes the upgrade name, a rank shown as a number followed by "/" and its cap, and a price number after the rank text.
The upgrades menu is displaying a maxed upgrade row → That upgrade row label includes the upgrade name and its cap rank shown as cap-number, "/", cap-number, with no price number after the rank text.
An upgrade row is selected from the upgrades menu → The selected upgrade row is visibly highlighted, and the flavor-description panel displays text for that selected upgrade.
A straight road segment is visible ahead during active running gameplay → The visible rainbow road continues forward without a lateral bend through that segment.
A screen-left curving road segment is visible ahead during active running gameplay → The visible rainbow road bends toward the screen-left side through that segment.
A low obstacle is present ahead in a lane during active running gameplay → A short block-like obstacle appears close to the road surface in that lane, with open space above it.
A high obstacle is present ahead in a lane during active running gameplay → An overhead obstacle appears in that lane with a visible gap between the road surface and the obstacle body.
A gate obstacle is present ahead in a lane during active running gameplay → A gate-shaped obstacle appears in that lane with side posts, a horizontal bar, and an additional upper block above the bar.
A tower obstacle is present ahead in a lane during active running gameplay → A tall solid obstacle rises from the road surface in that lane with no visible under-gap.

games.summaryZh: Rainbowhoof is a pastel side-scrolling runner about a unicorn galloping across terrain, gaps, spikes, and floating stardust. The player starts a run from a title screen, draws rainbow bridges with pointer or touch input to carry the unicorn through the course, manages a regenerating rainbow-ink meter, chains mid-air rainbow landings for combo multipliers, collects stardust for score and ink, and tries to travel farther and beat the saved best score before hitting spikes or falling into the void.

requirements.zh: The game page has completed its initial setup on a non-touch presentation before any player input → The title screen is rendered with the start prompt text "CLICK or SPACE" and the instruction line "chain rainbows mid-air to raise the multiplier - stardust refills your ink" visible over the animated game scene.

The title screen is rendered after its intro title animation has appeared → A rainbow-styled "RAINBOWHOOF" title is visible near the upper middle of the screen, with the subtitle "drag to paint a rainbow - then gallop on it" below it.

A pointer press is accepted while the title screen is showing → The title screen is replaced by active gameplay: the title prompt is no longer visible, the gameplay HUD is visible, and the run begins with the score display reset to 0.

An active gameplay frame is rendered → The play area is filled by a pastel vertical sky gradient, a pale circular sun glow appears in the upper-right sky, white star specks appear in the upper sky, and the screen edges are darkened by a purple vignette.

Active play is running from the starting distance and the unicorn advances forward without dying → The HUD distance readout changes from "0 m" to a nonzero value ending in "m" within 3 seconds while the gameplay HUD remains visible.

Active play is running from the starting score and the unicorn advances forward without dying → The HUD score readout changes from 0 to a value above 10 within 8 seconds while the side-scrolling terrain continues moving across the view.
The gameplay HUD is rendered while no stardust refill feedback is active → The HUD shows a "RAINBOW INK" label next to the ink bar and a numeric percentage text at the right side of the ink bar.
The HUD is rendered while the rainbow ink meter is full → The HUD ink bar is completely filled and has a translucent white sheen drawn across the full fill area.

Active play advances through an update while the HUD ink meter is below full and no ink is being spent or refilled by stardust → Within 2 seconds, the right edge of the colored fill in the HUD ink bar is rendered to the right of its position at the start of the interval, and the "+STARDUST" text is not visible during the interval.
The gameplay HUD is rendered while the saved best score is above 0 → The upper-right HUD shows a line beginning with "BEST" followed by a numeric score beneath the distance readout.
The gameplay HUD is rendered while the current chain multiplier is above 1 → A multiplier badge is visible in the HUD with an "x" followed by the multiplier number and the word "COMBO" below it.
