A drag gesture is accepted during active play while rainbow ink is available → A rainbow-colored bridge stroke appears along the dragged path in the gameplay scene.

A draw start is attempted during active play while the rainbow ink amount is below the drawing threshold → A red outline appears around the HUD ink bar, and no new in-progress rainbow stroke appears at the attempted start point.

An active rainbow drawing receives a valid drag segment while enough rainbow ink remains for that segment → The in-progress rainbow stroke extends to the new segment endpoint, and on at least one frame within 1 second the HUD ink percentage is at least 1 percentage point below its pre-segment value.

An active rainbow drawing receives a drag segment whose ink cost exceeds the remaining rainbow ink → The in-progress rainbow stroke stops before the drag endpoint, the HUD ink bar fill reaches empty, and a red outline appears around the HUD ink bar.

A rainbow drawing is released during active play after the stroke meets the minimum valid length → A persistent glowing rainbow bridge remains along the released path after the pointer is no longer down.

A rainbow drawing is released during active play after a stroke shorter than the minimum valid length → The transient in-progress rainbow stroke disappears, and no persistent rainbow bridge remains along the released path.
A rainbow bridge reaches the end of its lifetime during active play → That rainbow bridge is no longer visible in the gameplay scene.
The unicorn reaches the edge of a terrain gap while running on dirt during active play → The unicorn leaves the ground and moves through open air beyond the terrain edge.

The dirt-running unicorn reaches an upward dirt crest whose launch condition is met → The unicorn leaves the dirt surface and becomes airborne above continuous dirt terrain, without a terrain gap at the takeoff point.
The unicorn encounters a valid rainbow arc while running on dirt during active play → The unicorn transfers from the dirt terrain onto the rainbow arc and is shown riding along the rainbow bridge.
The airborne unicorn lands on a newly reached rainbow arc while the current chain count is zero → A spark particle burst appears at the unicorn, and the unicorn is shown riding on the rainbow arc.

The airborne unicorn lands on a newly reached rainbow arc while the current chain count is at least one → A spark particle burst appears at the unicorn, the unicorn is shown riding on the rainbow arc, and the HUD displays a chain multiplier label with an x followed by a number of 2 or above.
The unicorn reaches the end of the rainbow arc it is riding during active play → The unicorn leaves the rainbow arc and continues through open air beyond the arc endpoint.
The rainbow arc currently carrying the unicorn fades below its support threshold during active play → The unicorn leaves the rainbow arc and is shown moving through open air.

The unicorn riding a rainbow arc reaches an upward curve whose launch condition is met before the arc endpoint → The unicorn leaves the rainbow bridge from the curved section and continues through open air while the rainbow bridge remains visible behind it.

The airborne unicorn lands on dirt during active play while no chain multiplier label is visible → A dust particle burst appears at the unicorn's hooves, and the unicorn resumes running along the dirt terrain.

The unicorn lands on dirt during active play while a chain multiplier label is visible → A dust particle burst appears at the unicorn's hooves, and the chain multiplier label is no longer visible in the HUD within 1 second.
A new void terrain segment enters the gameplay view during active play → The dirt terrain is interrupted by a visible open gap with abyss showing between the terrain sections.
A spike obstacle generated on solid terrain enters the gameplay view during active play → A cluster of purple triangular spikes is visible on the dirt terrain.
A regular stardust pickup generated above the course enters the gameplay view → A glowing star-shaped stardust pickup is visible above the terrain or path.
A stardust pickup generated for a void gap enters the gameplay view → A glowing star-shaped stardust pickup floats over the open gap.

The unicorn intersects a stardust pickup during active play while no chain multiplier is active → The stardust pickup disappears, a star-shaped particle burst appears at the pickup position, and the HUD score readout increases by at least 50 from its pre-pickup value within 1 second.

The unicorn intersects a stardust pickup during active play while a chain multiplier label is visible → The stardust pickup disappears, a star-shaped particle burst appears at the pickup position, and the HUD score readout increases by at least 100 from its pre-pickup value within 1 second.

The unicorn intersects a stardust pickup during active play while the HUD ink bar is not full → The stardust pickup disappears, a star-shaped particle burst appears at the pickup position, and the ink HUD shows the text "+STARDUST" within 1 second.
The unicorn contacts a spike obstacle during active play → A boom particle burst appears at the unicorn, and the game-over overlay appears over the gameplay view.
The unicorn falls below the death boundary during active play → A boom particle burst appears at the unicorn, and the game-over overlay appears over the gameplay view.
The game-over presentation is rendered → A "GAME OVER" title is visible above a central panel labeled "SCORE" with the run's numeric score displayed in the panel.

The game-over screen has been displayed long enough for its retry prompt on a non-touch presentation → The game-over presentation shows the prompt text "CLICK or SPACE to retry" near the lower part of the screen.
The game-over presentation is rendered after a spike death → The game-over overlay shows the reason text "impaled on the spikes" below the main game-over title.
The game-over presentation is rendered after a void-fall death → The game-over overlay shows the reason text "lost to the void" below the main game-over title.
A game-over summary is rendered for a positive-score run whose score is not below the saved best score → The game-over presentation shows the line "** NEW BEST **" below the displayed score.

A game-over summary is rendered for a run whose score is below the saved best score → The game-over presentation shows a summary line containing "BEST", a distance value ending in "m", and "TOP CHAIN x" below the displayed score.

A pointer press is accepted on the game-over screen after the restart delay has elapsed → The game-over overlay disappears, active gameplay returns, existing drawn rainbow arcs are gone, and the score display is reset to 0.
The R key is pressed during active play → Active gameplay restarts from a clean starting stretch: existing drawn rainbow arcs are gone and the score display is reset to 0.

games.summaryZh: A side-scrolling unicorn platform runner in which the player controls jumps while the unicorn advances through a continuous course of platforms, gaps, rain effects, and rainbow objects. The objective is to stay on the platforms and keep progressing as distance accumulates; falling off the course ends the run and shows a restartable end overlay. Progression is continuous, with generated platform patterns, visual effects, camera movement, and distance feedback supporting the core loop of timing jumps over hazards and gaps.

requirements.zh: The game has completed its initial page and play-scene setup → The rendered view is the active side-scrolling gameplay scene, with no title menu or mode-selection screen shown.
An active gameplay frame is rendered after the canvas has been set up → The gameplay area is filled with a solid tan background behind the platforms and character.

A grounded player character is in active gameplay with solid ground underfoot and no accepted jump starting on that frame → The unicorn runs to the right along the top of the platform while the gameplay scene remains active.
A grounded player character has an accepted jump opportunity during active gameplay → The player character leaves the ground and moves upward from its standing position.

A jump input is received while the player character is airborne in the rising jump state → The unicorn remains airborne in its current rising jump motion, with no separate second jump restart visible at that moment.
A non-jumping player character has no solid surface directly underneath during active gameplay → The player character enters a downward fall through the open space below.
A jumping player character reaches the end of its upward jump motion during active gameplay → The player character stops moving upward and begins moving downward.
A falling player character reaches the top surface of a solid platform during active gameplay → The player character stops descending and remains positioned on the platform surface.

A buffered jump input is still active when the player character reaches the grounded landing state → The player character immediately leaves the platform again in a new upward jump instead of remaining on the landing frame.

The player character overlaps a platform with a side collision as the shallowest collision axis during active gameplay → The unicorn is pushed to the side of the platform and remains outside the platform block instead of passing through its side.
A rising player character collides with the underside of a platform during active gameplay → The unicorn is blocked beneath the platform and does not pass upward through the platform block.
A non-rain-reactive platform is rendered in the gameplay view → The platform is drawn as a tiled rectangular block using the normal platform tile artwork.
A rain-reactive platform is rendered in the gameplay view → The platform is drawn with alternate platform tile artwork while retaining the same tiled rectangular platform shape.

The platform generator advances to a blank gap pattern during active gameplay progression → The upcoming course contains an empty horizontal gap between the end of one platform and the start of the next platform.
A generated platform has the rainbow-spawning label during active gameplay progression → A rainbow object sprite appears above the course near that generated platform.
The player character reaches the horizontal proximity zone around the rainbow object during active gameplay → The unicorn is drawn with its rainbow-proximity sprite appearance.
The player character moves outside the rainbow object's horizontal proximity zone during active gameplay → The unicorn is drawn with its normal sprite appearance.
The rain shower timer reaches its trigger point during active gameplay → Multiple raindrops appear near the top of the gameplay view and descend through the scene.
A falling raindrop reaches the top surface of a rain-reactive platform → The raindrop disappears at the platform surface and a splash effect appears at that contact point.

A falling raindrop reaches the top-surface height of a non-rain-reactive platform during active gameplay → The raindrop continues descending past the platform surface and no splash effect appears at that contact height.

The player character moves beyond the camera's right deadzone during active gameplay → The camera pans right so the platforms and background shift left across the viewport while the player remains visible.

The displayed rounded distance value reaches a new displayed value during active gameplay → Across the rendered frame where the update occurs, the visible "Distance: " readout changes from its immediately preceding numeric value and still ends with the "m" suffix.

The player character falls below the lower gameplay boundary during active gameplay while the end menu is not already showing → An end-menu overlay appears over the gameplay scene with a visible distance readout ending in "m".
The end menu is showing with reset enabled and a jump input is received → The end-menu overlay disappears and the gameplay scene restarts with the unicorn back in active play on a platform.

games.summaryZh: Tube Masters is a 3D endless corridor runner where the player steers a small avatar horizontally through a tube-like play space. The objective is to keep moving, collect score pickups and boost items, and avoid rigid obstacles that end the run. Play begins from a popup overlay, then the core loop alternates between lateral dodging, item collection, score and time accumulation, and automatic spawning and forward motion of objects. The presentation includes a fixed-size canvas, score, top-score and time HUDs, a game-over/start overlay, and an optional debug readout.

requirements.zh: The game page completes its initial HTML layout with the game canvas present → the page shows the heading "Tube Masters" above a game canvas that is 800 pixels wide and 600 pixels tall

The first gameplay world render occurs after the floor and side wall components have been created → the canvas shows a gray corridor-like play area with a gray floor plane extending forward and two darker gray side wall planes along the left and right sides
The start-game control is accepted while the popup overlay is visible → the popup overlay disappears from the rendered page and the gameplay canvas remains visible
A render update occurs while active play is stopped and the popup overlay is hidden → the popup overlay appears on the rendered page

A gameplay update processes Right input while the player is inside the lateral movement bounds → the player avatar shifts horizontally toward the right side of the play area on the next rendered frame
A gameplay update processes Left input while the player is inside the lateral movement bounds → the player avatar shifts horizontally toward the left side of the play area on the next rendered frame
A gameplay update processes Right input while the player is at or beyond the right-side movement limit → the player avatar remains at the same right-edge lateral position on the next rendered frame
A pickup item is generated during active play → a new pickup collectible is visible ahead of the player in the play area on the next rendered gameplay frame
An obstacle item is generated during active play → a new rigid obstacle is visible ahead of the player in the play area on the next rendered gameplay frame
A boost item is generated during active play → a new boost collectible is visible ahead of the player in the play area on the next rendered gameplay frame
A gameplay update moves an already visible non-player item while the boost timer is not positive → the item advances toward the player on the next rendered gameplay frame

A gameplay update moves an already visible non-player item while the boost timer is positive → during the following 1-second interval, the item advances toward the player by twice its screen-space travel distance from a 1-second unboosted interval at the same visible depth, with a 20% tolerance

The player intersects a pickup collectible during active play while the boost timer is not positive → the pickup collectible is absent from the next rendered frame, and the score HUD changes from its pre-contact number to a different number

The player intersects a pickup collectible during active play while the boost timer is positive → the pickup collectible is absent from the next rendered frame, and the score HUD changes from its pre-contact number to a different number
The player intersects a boost collectible during active play → the boost collectible is absent from the next rendered gameplay frame
The player intersects a rigid obstacle during active play → the Play! popup overlay is visible over the gameplay canvas

A gameplay render update occurs while the current score is greater than the stored top score → the score HUD shows a "Score:" label with the current score number, and the top-score HUD shows a "Top:" label with the same number

A gameplay render update occurs while the stored top score is greater than or equal to the current score → the score HUD shows a "Score:" label with the current score number, and the top-score HUD shows a "Top:" label with the stored top-score number

A gameplay render update occurs during active play after the elapsed session time has crossed into the next displayed second → the time HUD changes from its previous minute:second value to the next minute:second value on the rendered page
The game data is reset while the current score is nonzero → the score HUD shows "Score: 0" on the next rendered gameplay frame

The game data is reset while the player avatar is displaced from its starting lateral position → the player avatar appears back at its centered starting lateral position on the next rendered gameplay frame
The game data is reset while at least one obstacle item is present in the play area → the obstacle item that was present before the reset is absent from the next rendered gameplay frame
The game data is reset while at least one pickup collectible is present in the play area → the pickup collectible that was present before the reset is absent from the next rendered gameplay frame
The game data is reset while at least one boost collectible is present in the play area → the boost collectible that was present before the reset is absent from the next rendered gameplay frame

games.summaryZh: SpacePi is a space-themed defensive line-drawing game where the player protects a growing circular base from incoming enemy lines. The core loop is to choose a level, spend regenerating power by dragging with the mouse to draw defensive line segments, destroy enemy lines before they hit the base, collect coins and powerups, and survive until the base reaches its goal size. Progression is organized across 13 levels with saved best scores, perfect-completion markers, earned funds, and purchasable upgrades that improve power, base resilience, drops, and powerup duration.

requirements.zh: The game presentation has completed its initial page setup → A SpacePi main menu is visible over the game area, showing the title "SpacePi", an Overview section with objective and controls text, a guide map with labeled Defensive Line and Enemy Line examples, and buttons labeled "Play Game", "Overall Stats", and "Reset Game Data".
The player activates the Play Game control from the main menu → The main menu is replaced by a level-selection and upgrades menu for starting a game.

The player presses the spacebar during an active level while no menu is open → A pause menu appears with the heading "Level 1 Paused" for the first level and buttons labeled "Resume Level" and "Quit Level".
The player activates the Resume Level control on the pause menu → The pause menu disappears and the active level view is visible again.
The player activates the Quit Level control on the pause menu → The pause menu is replaced by the level-selection and upgrades menu.

The level-selection and upgrades menu is displayed → A level status line is visible showing completed-level and perfect-level counts in the format "#/13 Completed - #/13 Perfect", and the level list contains buttons labeled 1 through 13.
The level-selection and upgrades menu is displayed while at least one upgrade is not at its final level → The funds display shows a dollar sign followed by a numeric funds amount.
The level-selection and upgrades menu is displayed while every upgrade has reached its final level → The funds display shows the text "$ Maxed".
The player activates the Return to Menu control from the level-selection and upgrades menu → The level-selection and upgrades menu is replaced by the SpacePi main menu.
The level-selection menu is displayed with a level at or below the player's unlocked progression → That level button is shown in an enabled state.
The level-selection menu is displayed with a level above the player's unlocked progression → That level button is shown in a disabled state.
The player activates an enabled level button from the level-selection menu → The selected level starts and the gameplay playfield is shown.
The player activates a disabled level button from the level-selection menu → The level-selection and upgrades menu remains visible and the gameplay playfield does not replace it.
The level-selection menu is displayed for a level that has no saved best score → That level button's score area shows the empty-set symbol "∅".
The level-selection menu is displayed for a level that has a saved best score → That level button's score area shows a numeric best score.
The level-selection menu is displayed for a level completed with zero base hits → That level button shows its "P" perfect marker.
The level-selection and upgrades menu is displayed with a non-maxed upgrade whose next cost is affordable → That upgrade row shows a cost followed by the word "Available".

The level-selection and upgrades menu is displayed with a non-maxed upgrade whose next cost is not affordable → That upgrade row shows a cost followed by the word "Unavailable" and is shown in a disabled state.
The level-selection and upgrades menu is displayed with an upgrade that has reached its final level → That upgrade row shows the text "Maxed".

The player activates an upgrade control from the upgrades menu while that upgrade is disabled because it is unaffordable → The upgrades menu remains visible, the activated upgrade row shows "Unavailable", and the funds display is shown in a red not-enough feedback state.
The player activates an upgrade control from the upgrades menu while that upgrade is already maxed → The upgrades menu remains visible and that upgrade row continues to show "Maxed".
The player activates an available upgrade control whose purchase raises that upgrade to its final level → The upgrades menu remains visible and the activated upgrade row shows "Maxed".

The player activates an available upgrade control whose purchase leaves that upgrade below its final level and the next upgrade cost is affordable with the remaining funds → The upgrades menu remains visible and the activated upgrade row shows the next cost followed by the word "Available".

The player activates an available upgrade control whose purchase leaves that upgrade below its final level and the next upgrade cost is not affordable with the remaining funds → The upgrades menu remains visible and the activated upgrade row shows the next cost followed by the word "Unavailable" in a disabled state.

The active level gameplay HUD is rendered → The top HUD shows a Completion text value in the format "Completion: current/goal (percent%)", a Power text value in the format "Power: current/capacity (percent%)", and a Score label with a numeric score value.
The active level gameplay HUD is rendered while at least one upgrade is not at its final level → The top-right HUD shows the label "Profit" with a dollar amount below it.

The active level gameplay HUD is rendered while the base completion value is above zero and below the goal value → A horizontal completion meter is visible beneath the Completion text, with a colored filled segment that occupies part of the dark meter track and does not fill the full track width.

An active level is still in its initial delay period → A large level-start overlay is visible over the playfield, the base goal circle is still being drawn outward from the center, and no harmful enemy lines are visible.
An active level's initial delay period has ended → The large level-start overlay text is no longer visible, and the base goal circle is drawn at its full target radius.

An active level is past its initial delay while the base has not reached its goal and the level has not ended → Across consecutive gameplay frames, the base circle's outer edge moves outward from its center until it reaches the goal circle.

An active level has current power below its capacity and no unlimited-power powerup active → Across consecutive gameplay frames, the filled portion of the power meter extends toward the meter's full width until it reaches full.
An active level has current power at its capacity → The power meter is filled across its full visible width and remains full across consecutive gameplay frames.

The player holds a drag during an active level with the pointer within the current available power distance and no unlimited-power powerup active → The temporary defensive line preview is drawn from the drag starting point to the pointer position.
The player holds a drag during an active level while unlimited power is active → The temporary defensive line preview is drawn from the drag starting point to the pointer position.

The player holds a drag during an active level with the pointer beyond the current available power distance and no unlimited-power powerup active → The temporary defensive line preview is drawn only from the drag starting point to the available-power limit along the drag direction, and the preview endpoint is not at the pointer.

The player releases the mouse button after dragging a nonzero distance during an active level while no menu is open and no unlimited-power powerup is active and the current power can pay for the drawn line → A defensive line remains visible in the playfield after the mouse button is released.

The player releases the mouse button after dragging a nonzero distance during an active level while unlimited power is active → A defensive line remains visible in the playfield from the drag starting point to the release point.

The player releases the mouse button during an active level without moving the drag endpoint away from the drag start → No new defensive line appears in the playfield after the mouse button is released.
A new harmful enemy line is generated from the top edge of the playfield → A harmful line segment appears with one endpoint on the top border of the playfield and extends inward toward the base.
A visible harmful enemy line is present in active gameplay → Across consecutive gameplay frames, the harmful line alternates between two visible pulse states while moving toward the base.

A harmful enemy line endpoint reaches the base during an active level before the level has ended → The base is covered by a white flash overlay, and the enemy line that reached the base is no longer visible at the contact point.

A defensive line intersects a harmful enemy line during active gameplay → The defensive line and the harmful enemy line disappear, a circular blast effect appears at the intersection point, and debris particles appear along the destroyed line and at the intersection point.
A defeated harmful enemy line produces coins → At least one coin icon appears at the defeat location and moves away from that point.
A defeated harmful enemy line produces a powerup → A powerup icon appears at the defeat location.

An uncollected coin is within the magnet range of the pointer during active gameplay → Using the first observed frame as the baseline, within the following 1 second the distance between the coin center and the pointer is reduced by at least 5 pixels at the fixed 960x600 presentation, with a tolerance of 2 pixels.
An uncollected coin reaches the collection distance from the pointer during active gameplay → The coin disappears from the playfield.

An uncollected powerup is within the magnet range of the pointer during active gameplay → Using the first observed frame as the baseline, within the following 1 second the distance between the powerup icon center and the pointer is reduced by at least 3 pixels at the fixed 960x600 presentation, with a tolerance of 2 pixels.
An uncollected powerup reaches the collection distance from the pointer during active gameplay → The powerup icon disappears and the HUD displays a powerup text label with a horizontal timer bar.

An active powerup is in effect during gameplay and its timer is above zero → The HUD shows the active powerup name above a horizontal timer meter; using the first observed frame as the baseline, within the following 1 second the timer meter's filled segment right edge is at least 6 pixels to the left of its baseline position at the fixed 960x600 presentation, with a tolerance of 2 pixels.
An active powerup's timer reaches zero during gameplay → The powerup text label and horizontal timer bar disappear from the HUD.
An active unlimited-power powerup is in effect during gameplay → The power meter is displayed as full.
An active base-generation-boost powerup is in effect during gameplay → The base circle cycles through changing hues and an additional ring is drawn over the base.
An active slow-enemies powerup is in effect while harmful enemy lines are visible during gameplay → The harmful enemy lines are rendered in a blue powerup color.
An active coin-scatter powerup reaches its coin-spawn interval during gameplay while upgrades are not maxed → New coin icons appear in the playfield.

An active level ends successfully → The gameplay view is replaced by a Level Stats menu whose status line reads "Level 1 Completed Successfully" for the first level, with rows for Duration, Lines Created, Total Line Length, Base Hits, Powerups Collected, Coins Collected, Profit, and Score; the Retry Level button is not shown and the Return to Upgrades/Levels button is shown.

An active level ends in failure → The gameplay view is replaced by a Level Stats menu whose status line reads "Level 1 Failed" for the first level, with rows for Duration, Lines Created, Total Line Length, Base Hits, Powerups Collected, Coins Collected, Profit, and Score; the Retry Level button and Return to Upgrades/Levels button are shown.
An active level ends successfully with zero base hits → The Level Stats menu shows the Base Hits row as "0" followed by a "Perfect!" label.

An active level ends successfully with a score that becomes the saved best score for that level → The Level Stats menu shows the Score row with a numeric score, the note "(Lower is Better)", and a "New Best Score!" label.
An active level ends in failure after any scored play → The Level Stats menu shows the Score row with a numeric score followed by the note "(Not Applied)".
The player activates the Retry Level control from the Level Stats menu after a failed level → The Level Stats menu is replaced by a restarted gameplay playfield for the same level.
The player activates the Return to Upgrades/Levels control from the Level Stats menu → The Level Stats menu is replaced by the level-selection and upgrades menu.

The player activates the Return to Upgrades/Levels control from the Level Stats menu after the first successful completion of Level 1 → The Level Stats menu is replaced by the level-selection and upgrades menu, the level status line shows "1/13 Completed", and the Level 2 button is enabled.

The player activates the Return to Upgrades/Levels control from the Level Stats menu after the first successful zero-base-hit completion of Level 1 → The Level Stats menu is replaced by the level-selection and upgrades menu, the level status line shows "1/13 Perfect", and the Level 1 button shows its "P" perfect marker.

games.summaryZh: A 2D space exploration game where the player pilots a small character through a wraparound star field, conserves and replenishes energy, finds artifacts, charges incomplete planet nodes to complete planets, and avoids or overcomes red enemies. The core loop is thrusting and turning through space or moving on planet surfaces, absorbing energy masses, completing planets to gain helpful planet sprites, using map and help overlays for navigation, and progressing by converting hostile or incomplete planetary areas into completed worlds with companion support.

requirements.zh: The game has loaded into the initial preload screen before audio generation has been started → The screen displays the two-line prompt text "CLICK TO INITIALIZE" and "GENERATION SEQUENCE".
The initial preload screen is clicked while audio generation has not been started → The preload prompt changes to text beginning with "SOUNDS RENDERING..." followed by a number.

The preload screen is active after all sounds have finished rendering → The screen displays the two-line prompt text "ALL SOUNDS RENDERED." and "PRESS UP/W/Z TO CONTINUE", with a star field moving horizontally behind the prompt.
The title screen is rendered → A dark horizontal strip spans the bottom tenth of the screen, separated from the rest of the title screen by a horizontal line.
The title screen is initialized → Five planet-sprite companions are visible near the player character on the title screen.
The player releases the Up key on the title screen → The display changes from the title screen to the active gameplay view.
The active gameplay view is rendered → The bottom-right of the gameplay screen displays the control hint text "M MAP/STATS H TOGGLE HELP".
The player releases the M key during active gameplay while the minimap is hidden → A minimap overlay appears, showing a scaled star field with markers for world objects.
The player releases the M key during active gameplay while the minimap is displayed → The minimap overlay is removed from the gameplay view.
The player releases the H key during active gameplay while the help overlay is hidden → A help text overlay appears over the gameplay view.
The player releases the H key during active gameplay while the help overlay is displayed → The help text overlay disappears from the gameplay view.
The help overlay is displayed during active gameplay → The help overlay includes the two-line text "HUD INDICATES" and "NEARBY PLANETS" next to a circular HUD diagram.

The help overlay is displayed while the player is not near a planet, is not being drained, has fuel below 5, and the low-fuel blink interval is active → The help overlay displays the three-line message "FIND ENERGY MASS TO ABSORB", "OR TRAVEL NEAR COMPLETE PLANETS", and "TO RECHARGE".

The help overlay is displayed while the player is within an incomplete planet's gravity field, that planet has at least one harvester, and the player is not being drained → The help overlay displays the two-line message "THE RED CAN ONLY" and "BE KILLED BY PLANET SPRITES".

The help overlay is displayed while the player is within an incomplete planet's gravity field, that planet has no harvesters, the charge-up help interval is active, and the player is not being drained → The help overlay displays the two-line message "CHARGE UP PLANET NODES" and "TO COMPLETE PLANETS".

The help overlay is displayed while the player is within an incomplete planet's gravity field, that planet has no harvesters, the planet-sprite reward help interval is active, and the player is not being drained → The help overlay displays the two-line message "COMPLETING A PLANET GIVES" and "YOU A PLANET SPRITE".

The help overlay is displayed while the player is within a completed planet's gravity field, the recharge help interval is active, and the player is not being drained → The help overlay displays the two-line message "COMPLETED PLANETS RECHARGE" and "YOUR ENERGY WHEN CLOSE".
The help overlay is displayed while the player is being drained by a red enemy → The help overlay displays the two-line message "THE RED DRAIN YOUR ENERGIES" and "KEEP YOUR DISTANCE".

The gameplay HUD is drawn while the player's fuel is at maximum → A horizontal fuel bar is visible near the top center of the gameplay screen, with the colored filled segment extending across the full dark backing bar.

The gameplay HUD is drawn while the player's fuel is above zero and below maximum → A horizontal fuel bar is visible near the top center of the gameplay screen, with the colored filled segment starting at the left edge of the dark backing bar and ending before the backing bar's right edge.
The gameplay HUD is drawn while the player's fuel is zero → A horizontal dark backing bar is visible near the top center of the gameplay screen with no colored filled segment visible inside it.

The Left arrow key is held during active gameplay while the player is in open space outside planet gravity → Across consecutive gameplay frames, the player character rotates counterclockwise and a particle burst appears at one arm.

The Right arrow key is held during active gameplay while the player is in open space outside planet gravity → Across consecutive gameplay frames, the player character rotates clockwise and a particle burst appears at the opposite arm.

The Up arrow key is held during active gameplay while the player is in open space outside planet gravity → Across consecutive gameplay frames, the player moves in the direction they are facing and paired particle bursts appear at the feet.

The Down arrow key is held during active gameplay while the player is in open space outside planet gravity → Across consecutive gameplay frames, the player moves backward relative to the direction they are facing and particle bursts appear at both arms.

The Left arrow key is held while the player is standing on a planet surface → Across consecutive gameplay frames, the player changes position along the planet surface in one tangential direction, and no jet particle burst appears from the player.

The Right arrow key is held while the player is standing on a planet surface → Across consecutive gameplay frames, the player changes position along the planet surface in the opposite tangential direction from Left-arrow surface movement, and no jet particle burst appears from the player.
The Up arrow key is held while the player is standing on a planet surface → The player jumps outward from the planet surface.
The Down arrow key is held while the player is standing on a planet surface → The player remains on the planet surface and no jet particle burst appears from the player during the input.
A collectible artifact is within the normal gameplay view → The artifact is drawn at its world position as a cluster of colored rectangular blocks.
The player overlaps a collectible artifact during active gameplay → The artifact disappears and a burst of particles appears at its position.
At least one artifact has been collected when the collected-artifacts display is drawn → A colored square with a thin outline appears near the bottom-left of the screen for each collected artifact.

The player is within absorption range of an energy mass while the player's fuel is below maximum → The energy mass shows a reaching effect toward the player; by the end of a 1-second observation interval, the energy mass circle has at least a 3 in-game-pixel smaller visible radius than it had at the beginning of the interval.

The player is within absorption range of an energy mass while the player's fuel is at maximum → The energy mass keeps its pre-contact visible radius for the next 1 second and no reaching effect is drawn from the energy mass toward the player.
An energy mass reaches zero visible radius after being absorbed → The energy mass disappears and a particle burst appears at its position.
An incomplete planet is within the normal gameplay view → The planet is drawn without a colored atmospheric halo and has a red body outline plus a thin outer gravity-field ring.

The player is within charging range of an incomplete planet node while the player has fuel remaining and the node is below its full size → The node shows a reaching effect toward the player; within 0.5 seconds after the condition is reached, the node's visible circle radius increases by at least 1 in-game pixel from its radius at the beginning of the interval.

The player is within charging range of an incomplete planet node while the player has no fuel remaining → The node keeps its pre-contact visible radius for the next 1 second and no reaching effect is drawn from the node toward the player.
An incomplete planet node exceeds its full charge size → The node stops appearing as an uncompleted energy mass and a particle burst appears at its position.
A planet's final incomplete node has just been completed → The planet changes to its completed appearance with a colored atmospheric halo around it.
The player is close enough to a completed planet for its recharge reach effect → The completed planet displays a reaching visual effect around its halo toward the player.
A planet is outside the normal gameplay view but within the radar indicator range → An off-screen planet indicator appears near the edge of the gameplay view in the direction of that planet.
The minimap is displayed while an incomplete planet is present → The incomplete planet appears on the minimap as a small marker without an outline ring.
The minimap is displayed while a completed planet is present → The completed planet appears on the minimap as a colored marker with an outline ring.
The minimap is displayed during a frame when the player marker is enabled → The player's position is marked on the minimap by a cluster of bright pixels.

A red drone is within its approach range during active gameplay → Over a 1-second observation interval with the player visible, the red drone's screen-space position shifts toward the player's screen-space position by at least 1 in-game pixel.
The player is within a red drone's drain range during active gameplay → The red drone displays reaching tendrils toward the player and drain particles appear around the player.
The player contacts a red drone at low speed while the player's fuel is above 100 → A burst of concentric explosion rings appears at the red drone's position.

A red drone's health reaches zero → The red drone disappears from the gameplay view, a burst of explosion rings appears at the red drone's position, and five energy masses appear around the former drone position.
A red harvester is alive and attached to its planet during active gameplay → Over a 1-second observation interval, the red harvester is visible at different positions on the planet's perimeter.
A red harvester is within its drain range during active gameplay → The red harvester displays reaching tendrils toward the player and drain particles appear around the player.
The player contacts a red harvester at low speed → A particle burst appears at the harvester and the player is knocked away from the contact point.

A red harvester's health reaches zero → The red harvester disappears from the gameplay view, a burst of explosion rings appears at the red harvester's position, and two energy masses appear around the former harvester position.
A planet sprite has no red enemy in view and the player is outside planet gravity → The planet sprite is visible near the player as a colored circular body with trail particles.

A planet sprite has no red enemy in view while the player is within a planet gravity field → Over a 1-second observation interval, the planet sprite is visible at different positions around the planet, with a colored circular body and trail particles.

A planet sprite has a red enemy in view while it is not already attacking → The planet sprite moves away from its following or orbiting position to circle the red enemy, and it is drawn with a red-orange outline and trail.
The player's world position crosses beyond the right boundary of the world → The gameplay view jumps to the left side of the world, with the player still visible after the wrap.
The player's world position crosses beyond the bottom boundary of the world → The gameplay view jumps to the top side of the world, with the player still visible after the wrap.

games.summaryZh: Lost Robot is a top-down robot navigation puzzle game about steering a small robot through selectable maze-like maps. The player uses differential drive controls to move and rotate the robot, collects point items, opens doors when linked pickups are collected, avoids obstacle collisions that reduce score, and tries to reach the cyan goal quickly. The game starts from a title screen, moves through a map selection screen that displays saved scores and times, then runs timed gameplay with a visible HUD and returns to map selection after a level is completed.

requirements.zh: The game page is first presented before startup initialization has enabled play → A full-screen title screen is visible with the heading "LOST ROBOT" and a disabled start button labeled "Loading … Please wait."
Startup initialization completes while the title screen is shown → The title screen remains visible and the start button label changes to "Start".
The enabled Start button is activated on the title screen → The title screen is hidden and the "CHOOSE A MAP" level selection screen is shown.

The level selection menu is populated while the level selection screen is being shown → Under the "CHOOSE A MAP" heading, the screen displays map selection buttons whose visible labels include a map number line, a "Points:" line, and a "Time:" line.
The level selection menu is populated for a map that has a saved completion state → That map's selection button shows a "Time:" line in MM:SS:mmm format with at least one digit from 1 through 9.
A level is selected from the level selection screen → The level selection screen is hidden and the gameplay view is shown.

A level has begun and the robot is not disabled while the map timer is running → The gameplay HUD shows a time readout in the upper-left corner of the canvas and a points readout below the time readout.

The map timer continues running during active gameplay while the robot is enabled → The visible time readout advances; within 2 seconds of gameplay video, the seconds portion of the time display increases by at least 1.
A gameplay map is rendered during active play → The robot is visible in the playfield.
A gameplay map containing the goal is rendered before the robot reaches the goal radius → A cyan circular goal marker is visible at the goal location in the playfield.

The robot enters the goal radius while it is enabled during active play → A white overlay is visible over the gameplay canvas, and the time and points readouts are drawn inside the central half of the canvas.
The scheduled post-goal return delay elapses after the robot has reached the goal → The gameplay view is hidden and the level selection screen is shown.
The Escape key is accepted during active gameplay while the robot is enabled → The gameplay view is hidden and the level selection screen is shown.

The camera mode toggle is newly accepted during active gameplay while fixed camera mode is active → The gameplay camera switches to robot-relative view, with the map rotated so the robot's current heading is oriented upward in the view.

The camera mode toggle is newly accepted during active gameplay while robot-relative camera mode is active → The gameplay camera switches back to fixed-map view, with the map drawn in its normal unrotated orientation instead of being kept aligned to the robot heading.

During active gameplay, the robot receives equal forward acceleration on its left and right drives → While the condition is maintained, the robot body translates in the direction its nose faces and its orientation stays unchanged.

During active gameplay, the robot receives equal backward acceleration on its left and right drives → While the condition is maintained, the robot body translates opposite the direction its nose faces and its orientation stays unchanged.

During active gameplay, the robot receives forward acceleration on the left drive and backward acceleration on the right drive → While the condition is maintained, the robot rotates right in place without translating across the map.

During active gameplay, the robot receives backward acceleration on the left drive and forward acceleration on the right drive → While the condition is maintained, the robot rotates left in place without translating across the map.
During active gameplay, the robot receives forward acceleration on only the left drive → While the condition is maintained, the robot turns right while translating forward.
During active gameplay, the robot receives forward acceleration on only the right drive → While the condition is maintained, the robot turns left while translating forward.
During active gameplay, the robot receives backward acceleration on only the left drive → While the condition is maintained, the robot turns left while translating backward.
During active gameplay, the robot receives backward acceleration on only the right drive → While the condition is maintained, the robot turns right while translating backward.
During active gameplay, the robot receives no nonzero drive acceleration → While the condition is maintained, the robot's visible position and orientation remain unchanged.
During active gameplay, the left robot drive has nonzero forward acceleration while the robot is rendered → An arrow is drawn on the left drive pointing toward the robot's front.
During active gameplay, the left robot drive has nonzero backward acceleration while the robot is rendered → An arrow is drawn on the left drive pointing toward the robot's rear.
During active gameplay, the left robot drive has zero acceleration while the robot is rendered → No arrow is drawn on the left drive.
The robot collides with an obstacle while the point-loss cooldown is expired → The visible points readout decreases by 10 from its pre-collision value.
The robot collides with an obstacle while the point-loss cooldown is active → The visible points readout remains unchanged during that collision.

The robot enters the pickup radius of an uncollected collectible that has no active door-opening trigger listener → The collectible changes from a filled circle to a hollow shell, and the visible points readout increases by 100.

The robot enters the pickup radius of an uncollected collectible that has an active door-opening trigger listener → The collectible changes from a filled circle to a hollow shell, the visible points readout increases by 100, and the linked door changes from a blocking door segment to an open gap.
An open door's closed state is applied during gameplay → The open gap changes back into a visible blocking door segment.
The robot moves while turbo mode is active → Colored trail segments appear behind the robot as it moves.
Movement input is received while the robot is disabled after reaching the goal → The robot remains stationary while the white fade overlay remains on the gameplay view.

games.summaryZh: A top-down survival exploration game about being stranded on an island. The player starts from a story screen, enters a scrolling tile-map world, searches the terrain for food and three rescue-radio parts, and uses keyboard movement plus an action check to gather nearby items. The core loop is to navigate land while avoiding impassable water and map edges, watch the proximity indicator and hunger hearts, collect resources, and either assemble the rescue equipment to be saved or starve and reach a game-over ending.

requirements.zh: The page has completed its initial startup display before the game has started → The start screen is visible with the title "Lost", story and control instructions, and the prompt "Press space to start"; the gameplay canvas and ending messages are not visible.
A keypress is received while the start screen is active → The start screen disappears and the gameplay view appears.

The player's hunger/health reaches zero during active play → The gameplay view disappears and a message screen appears with the heading "Game Over" and the text "You died from starvation. No one ever found you. You are lost forever."

During active play, the objective check runs with the transmitter, antenna, and battery all collected → The gameplay view disappears and a message screen appears with the heading "Rescued" and the text "A fishing boat get your call and is on its way to get you. Seems you are not lost after all :)."

During active play, the player has an upward movement input, no horizontal movement input, and the computed destination is a valid land position → Across consecutive gameplay frames, the surrounding terrain shifts downward relative to the player character.

During active play, the player has a downward movement input, no horizontal movement input, and the computed destination is a valid land position → Across consecutive gameplay frames, the surrounding terrain shifts upward relative to the player character.

During active play, the player has a rightward movement input, no vertical movement input, and the computed destination is a valid land position → Across consecutive gameplay frames, the surrounding terrain shifts left relative to the player character.

During active play, the player has a leftward movement input, no vertical movement input, and the computed destination is a valid land position → Across consecutive gameplay frames, the surrounding terrain shifts right relative to the player character.

During active play, the player has simultaneous upward and rightward movement inputs and the computed destination is a valid land position → Across consecutive gameplay frames, the surrounding terrain shifts down and left relative to the player character.

During active play, the player's computed movement destination is beyond the left edge of the world map → The player character does not advance beyond the visible world edge; consecutive gameplay frames show no displacement into off-map space.

During active play, the player's computed movement destination is on a water-height tile → The player character does not enter the water tile; consecutive gameplay frames show the player remaining on the adjacent land tile.
During active play, the action check finds an apple tree in the player's pickup tiles → The apple tree graphic is removed from its terrain tile on the following gameplay frames.
During active play, the action check finds a berry bush in the player's pickup tiles → The berry bush graphic is removed from its terrain tile on the following gameplay frames.

During active play, the action check finds the transmitter in the player's pickup tiles and this pickup does not complete all required rescue parts → The transmitter graphic is removed from its terrain tile, the transmitter row in the equipment HUD reads "1 x" next to the transmitter icon, and the gameplay view remains visible.

During active play, the action check finds the antenna in the player's pickup tiles and this pickup does not complete all required rescue parts → The antenna graphic is removed from its terrain tile, the antenna row in the equipment HUD reads "1 x", and the gameplay view remains visible.

During active play, the action check finds the battery in the player's pickup tiles and this pickup does not complete all required rescue parts → The battery graphic is removed from its terrain tile, the battery row in the equipment HUD reads "1 x", and the gameplay view remains visible.

During active play, the action check finds no food, transmitter, antenna, or battery in the player's pickup tiles → The gameplay view remains visible and no nearby collectible graphic is removed after the action check.
During active play, the player is less than 500 world units from the current objective item when the player indicator is rendered → The small objective indicator on the player is red.

During active play, the player is at least 500 and less than 1000 world units from the current objective item when the player indicator is rendered → The small objective indicator on the player is orange.

During active play, the player is at least 1000 and less than 2000 world units from the current objective item when the player indicator is rendered → The small objective indicator on the player is yellow.

During active play, the player is at least 2000 and less than 3000 world units from the current objective item when the player indicator is rendered → The small objective indicator on the player is blue.
During active play, the player is at least 3000 world units from the current objective item when the player indicator is rendered → The small objective indicator on the player is dark blue.
During active play, a visible map tile with height 0 is rendered in the gameplay viewport → That tile is drawn with the deep ocean terrain graphic.
During active play, a visible map tile with height 2 is rendered in the gameplay viewport → That tile is drawn with the coast terrain graphic.
During active play, a visible map tile with height 4 is rendered in the gameplay viewport → That tile is drawn with the sand terrain graphic.
During active play, a visible map tile with height 5 is rendered in the gameplay viewport → That tile is drawn with the grass terrain graphic.
During active play, a visible map tile with height 6 is rendered in the gameplay viewport → That tile is drawn with the forest terrain graphic.
During active play, a visible map tile with a berry bush is rendered in the gameplay viewport → A berry bush graphic is drawn on that terrain tile.
During active play, a visible map tile with a palm tree is rendered in the gameplay viewport → A palm tree graphic is drawn over that terrain tile.
During active play, a visible map tile with an apple tree is rendered in the gameplay viewport → An apple tree graphic is drawn over that terrain tile.
During active play, a visible map tile with the transmitter is rendered in the gameplay viewport → A transmitter graphic is drawn on that terrain tile.
During active play, a visible map tile with the antenna is rendered in the gameplay viewport → An antenna graphic is drawn on that terrain tile.
During active play, a visible map tile with the battery is rendered in the gameplay viewport → A battery graphic is drawn on that terrain tile.
During active play, the player character is rendered in the gameplay viewport → A small humanoid player figure is drawn at the center of the gameplay canvas.
During active play, the health display is rendered while the player's rounded heart count is positive → The top-left health display contains heart symbols.

During active play, the equipment HUD is rendered → Three equipment rows are visible near the right edge of the gameplay canvas: a transmitter icon row, an antenna icon row below it, and a battery icon row below the antenna row, each with white count text to its left.
During active play, the equipment HUD is rendered while the player does not have the transmitter → The transmitter row in the equipment HUD reads "0 x" next to the transmitter icon.

During active play, the hunger timer reaches its one-second decrease point while the resulting rounded heart count is exactly one lower than the previous rounded heart count and the player remains alive → The health display at the top-left shows one fewer heart symbol than it showed before the decrease, and the gameplay view remains visible.

During active play, the action check finds a food tile in the player's pickup tiles and the resulting rounded heart count is exactly one higher than the previous rounded heart count → The health display at the top-left shows one additional heart symbol compared with the display before the action check.

games.summaryZh: A 2D adventure platformer about rescuing a lost friend trapped in a portal. The player explores a central water hub, talks with island guardians, unlocks elemental islands, collects four gems from themed air, earth, fire, and river challenges, then places the gems into the central portal. Play combines keyboard movement, jumping and double-jumping, obstacle avoidance, enemy and hazard encounters, health management, dialog navigation, level transitions, and final progression to a victory menu.

requirements.zh: The game reaches its first rendered frame after initial page setup → A centered menu screen is visible with the title text "Save the Lost Friend".

The main menu is drawn before the game has been completed → Below the title, the menu shows the instruction text "Talk to the 4 guardians and get the keys to the 4 islands. Get the gems from the 4 islands." and "Place the gems in the circular portal in central island to rescue your lost friend".

The pre-victory menu is drawn before the game has been completed → The menu shows the heading "Controls", the text "Arrow keys for movement, Up arrow to fly and double jump.", the text "Enter key to proceed in dialog, Esc key to exit dialog.", and a turquoise rectangle containing "Press P to play".
A playable level begins after its display and HUD are created → A centered gameplay canvas is visible with an in-game HUD showing a health bar.
A gameplay HUD frame is drawn during an active level → A pale beige HUD strip spans the bottom of the display, and the text "Press P for Help" is visible near the lower-right corner.
The HUD draws while the player's health equals its maximum health → The bar labeled "Health" is filled green across its full visible width with no red segment visible.
A nonempty HUD game message is active when the HUD draws → A translucent white rectangular message backdrop with a grey inner rectangle is visible, with the message text centered inside it.
A horizontal platformer level begins after its display and HUD are created → The HUD shows a progress bar labeled "Progress" in addition to the health bar.
A vertical platformer level begins after its display and HUD are created → The HUD shows a progress bar labeled "Progress" in addition to the health bar.
A non-platformer level begins after its display and HUD are created → The HUD shows the health bar and does not show a progress bar labeled "Progress".

A horizontal platformer HUD draws while the player's horizontal progress is at least half of the level width → The progress bar labeled "Progress" is filled to at least one half of its full visible width.
A vertical platformer HUD draws while the player's upward progress is at least half of the level height → The progress bar labeled "Progress" is filled to at least one half of its full visible width.

During active platformer play, the left movement control is held while the player's next horizontal step has no obstacle → The player advances left through the level between consecutive gameplay frames.

During active platformer play, the right movement control is held while the player's next horizontal step has no obstacle → The player advances right through the level between consecutive gameplay frames.

During active platformer play, the jump control is held as the player lands on a solid obstacle while falling → The player reverses from downward motion to upward motion and begins a jump on the following gameplay frames.

During active platformer play, the jump control is held while the player is airborne with double jump enabled and not already moving upward faster than the double-jump threshold → The player changes from falling or shallow upward motion into a new upward jump on the following gameplay frames.
During active platformer play, the player is airborne with downward vertical speed and the next vertical step has no obstacle → The player moves downward between consecutive gameplay frames.
The player attempts a horizontal platformer move whose next position intersects a solid obstacle → The player remains outside the solid obstacle and does not pass through its visible boundary.

During active platformer play, the player collides vertically with a solid obstacle without starting a jump → The player remains outside the solid obstacle and stops vertical travel at the obstacle boundary on the following gameplay frames.
During active non-platformer play, the left movement control is held while the player's next step has no obstacle → The player advances left through the level between consecutive gameplay frames.
During active non-platformer play, the right movement control is held while the player's next step has no obstacle → The player advances right through the level between consecutive gameplay frames.
During active non-platformer play, the up movement control is held while the player's next step has no obstacle → The player advances upward through the level between consecutive gameplay frames.
During active non-platformer play, the down movement control is held while the player's next step has no obstacle → The player advances downward through the level between consecutive gameplay frames.
During active non-platformer play, the player's next step intersects a solid obstacle → The player remains outside the solid obstacle and does not pass through its visible boundary.

During active earth level play before the far-right end section, the player's next automatic horizontal step has no obstacle → The player advances right through the level between consecutive gameplay frames.
The player crosses the left camera margin in a scrollable level → The level scenery shifts right between consecutive frames while the player remains visible in the gameplay canvas.
The player crosses the right camera margin in a scrollable level → The level scenery shifts left between consecutive frames while the player remains visible in the gameplay canvas.
The player crosses the upper camera margin in a scrollable level → The level scenery shifts downward between consecutive frames while the player remains visible in the gameplay canvas.
The player crosses the lower camera margin in a scrollable level → The level scenery shifts upward between consecutive frames while the player remains visible in the gameplay canvas.

The player is drawn while facing right and their hit timer is inactive → The player appears as a gold vertical body with a black eye on the right side of the face and a black mouth mark extending across the right half of the body.

The player is drawn while facing left and their hit timer is inactive → The player appears as a gold vertical body with a black eye on the left side of the face and a black mouth mark extending across the left half of the body.
The player is drawn while their hit timer is active → The player's body is rendered with a translucent red fill instead of the normal gold fill.

The player touches a cactus while their health is 100 and their hit timer is inactive → The HUD displays the message "Beware of the cactus.", and within 1 second the green filled portion of the Health bar is between 75% and 85% of the bar's full visible width.

The player touches an evil cloud while their health is 100 and their hit timer is inactive → The HUD displays the message "Beware of the Evil Cloud.", and within 1 second the green filled portion of the Health bar is between 45% and 55% of the bar's full visible width.

The player touches volcanic lava while their health is 100 and their hit timer is inactive → The HUD displays the message "Beware of the Volcanic Lava.", and within 1 second the green filled portion of the Health bar is between 45% and 55% of the bar's full visible width.

The player touches a fire bolt while their health is 100, their hit timer is inactive, and the fire level is still active → The HUD displays the message "Beware of the Fire Bolt.", and within 1 second the green filled portion of the Health bar is between 45% and 55% of the bar's full visible width.

The player touches a shark while their health is 100, their hit timer is inactive, and no dialog interaction is active → The HUD displays the message "Shark Attacked. 90", and within 1 second the green filled portion of the Health bar is between 85% and 95% of the bar's full visible width.

The player touches a cactus while their hit timer is active → The health bar's filled portion keeps the same visible length for the next 1 second and no new HUD message "Beware of the cactus." appears.

The player touches a cactus in the earth level while their health is 20 and their hit timer is inactive → The level enters the lost-state animation: the player sprite begins moving downward and its visible body height begins shrinking.

The player touches an evil cloud in the air level while their health is 50 and their hit timer is inactive → The level enters the lost-state animation: the player sprite begins moving downward and its visible body height begins shrinking.

The player touches volcanic lava in the fire level while their health is 50 and their hit timer is inactive → The level enters the lost-state animation: the player sprite begins moving downward and its visible body height begins shrinking.

The player touches a fire bolt in the fire level while their health is 50 and their hit timer is inactive → The level enters the lost-state animation: the player sprite begins moving downward and its visible body height begins shrinking.

The player touches a shark in the water hub while their health is 10, their hit timer is inactive, and no dialog interaction is active → The level enters the lost-state animation: the player sprite begins moving downward and its visible body height begins shrinking.
A lost level reaches the end of its finish delay → The same level is shown again with the player restored to a starting position and a full health bar.
The player touches surface lava in the fire level while the level is still active → The HUD displays the message "Lava killed you.".
The player touches the fierce river hazard while the river level is still active → The HUD displays the message "Drowned in the fierce river.".
The river player overlaps a stationary standing platform during the river level → The player remains on the platform and the HUD does not display "Drowned in the fierce river.".

The player touches a berry in the fire level while their health is 90 → The berry sprite disappears, the HUD displays the message "Gained health", and the health bar's filled portion extends from nine tenths of the bar's full width to the full bar width within 1 second.
The player touches the air gem while the air level is still active → The air gem sprite disappears, and after the level win delay the water hub level replaces the air level on screen.

The player touches the earth stone gem while the earth level is still active → The earth stone gem sprite disappears and after the level win delay the water hub level replaces the earth level on screen.
The player touches the fire stone gem while the fire level is still active → The fire stone gem sprite disappears and after the level win delay the water hub level replaces the fire level on screen.
The player touches the river gem while the river level is still active → The river gem sprite disappears and after the level win delay the water hub level replaces the river level on screen.

A collected, unplaced water gem is accepted into the portal while fewer than three gems are already placed → A blue diamond appears at the lower-right area of the portal and the HUD displays a gem-placed message containing "water".

A collected, unplaced earth gem is accepted into the portal while fewer than three gems are already placed → A brown diamond appears at the lower-left area of the portal and the HUD displays a gem-placed message containing "earth".

A collected, unplaced air gem is accepted into the portal while fewer than three gems are already placed → A light gray diamond appears at the upper-left area of the portal and the HUD displays a gem-placed message containing "air".

A collected, unplaced fire gem is accepted into the portal while fewer than three gems are already placed → A red diamond appears at the upper-right area of the portal and the HUD displays a gem-placed message containing "fire".

The player touches the portal while no collected gem remains unplaced and fewer than four gems are placed → The portal display remains unchanged for the next 1 second and no new HUD gem-placed message appears.
The fourth gem is accepted into the portal → A centered menu screen is visible with the title text "Save the Lost Friend" and the message "You have Won.".

The post-victory menu is drawn after the game has been completed → The menu shows the title "Save the Lost Friend", the message "You have Won.", and the text "You have rescued your friend and others trapped in the portal".
The player touches the locked earth island entrance in the water hub → The HUD displays the message "You need to collect the key from crab to enter the earth island".
The player touches the locked water island entrance in the water hub → The HUD displays the message "You need to collect the key from tortoise to enter the water island".
The player touches the locked air island entrance in the water hub → The HUD displays the message "You need to collect the key from owl to enter the air island".
The player touches the locked fire island entrance in the water hub → The HUD displays the message "You need to collect the key from eagle to enter the fire island".
The player touches the earth island entrance in the water hub after the earth gem has already been collected → The HUD displays the message "You have already collected the gem from earth island".
The player touches the water island entrance in the water hub after the water gem has already been collected → The HUD displays the message "You have already collected the gem from water island".
The player touches the air island entrance in the water hub after the air gem has already been collected → The HUD displays the message "You have already collected the gem from air island".
The player touches the fire island entrance in the water hub after the fire gem has already been collected → The HUD displays the message "You have already collected the gem from fire island".

The player touches the unlocked earth island entrance in the water hub before the earth gem has been collected → The HUD displays the message "Welcome to the earth island" and, after the level transition delay, the earth level replaces the water hub on screen.

The player touches the unlocked water island entrance in the water hub before the water gem has been collected → The HUD displays the message "Welcome to the water island" and, after the level transition delay, the river level replaces the water hub on screen.

The player touches the unlocked air island entrance in the water hub before the air gem has been collected → The HUD displays the message "Welcome to the air island" and, after the level transition delay, the air level replaces the water hub on screen.

The player touches the unlocked fire island entrance in the water hub before the fire gem has been collected → The HUD displays the message "Welcome to the fire island" and, after the level transition delay, the fire level replaces the water hub on screen.
The pause control is released after being pressed during active gameplay → The gameplay view is replaced by a centered menu screen with the title text "Save the Lost Friend".
The pause control is released after being pressed while the pause menu is displayed during a level → The menu disappears and the playable level view with the in-game HUD is visible again.

A gameplay frame updates while a dialog interaction is active and a movement control is held → The player stays at the same visible playfield position while the dialog or question UI remains displayed.

The player collides with an NPC that has a question dialog while no question list is open → A dialog UI appears in the HUD area with question text entries, and one question entry is highlighted in red while the other visible entries are black.
The player collides with an NPC whose current dialog batch has no questions → The HUD displays a dialog welcome message without showing a red-highlighted question list.

The enter selection control is pressed while an NPC dialog is active before the question list is displayed → The HUD area changes from the dialog message to a question list with one entry highlighted in red.
The up selection control is pressed while a dialog question list is open and the first question is highlighted → The red highlight moves from the first question entry to the last question entry.
The down selection control is pressed while a dialog question list is open and the last question is highlighted → The red highlight moves from the last question entry to the first question entry.

The up selection control is pressed while a dialog question list is open and a non-first question is highlighted → The red highlight moves from the currently highlighted question entry to the question entry directly above it.

The down selection control is pressed while a dialog question list is open and a non-last question is highlighted → The red highlight moves from the currently highlighted question entry to the question entry directly below it.
The enter selection control is pressed while a dialog question list is open → The question list is replaced by the selected question's answer text in the HUD area.
The skip dialog control is pressed while an NPC dialog message is displayed → The dialog message text disappears from the HUD area and the normal gameplay HUD remains visible.
The skip dialog control is pressed while an NPC answer text is displayed → The answer text disappears from the HUD area and the normal gameplay HUD remains visible.
A dialog batch advances after every visible question in the current batch has been answered and another batch exists → A question list is displayed with the first question entry highlighted in red.
An evil cloud updates while its next position has no obstacle → The evil cloud sprite occupies a different position between consecutive gameplay frames.
An evil cloud updates while its next position intersects a solid obstacle → The evil cloud changes direction and moves back away from the obstacle on the following gameplay frames.
A moving log updates while its next position has no obstacle → The log sprite occupies a different horizontal position between consecutive gameplay frames.
A moving log updates while its next position intersects a solid obstacle → The log changes horizontal direction and moves back away from the obstacle on the following gameplay frames.
The river player overlaps a moving log during the river level → The player is carried horizontally with the moving log on the following gameplay frames.
A shark updates while its next position has no obstacle or island → The shark sprite occupies a different position between consecutive gameplay frames.
A shark updates while its next position intersects a solid obstacle → The shark changes direction and moves back away from the obstacle on the following gameplay frames.
A shark updates while its next position intersects an island → The shark changes direction and moves back away from the island on the following gameplay frames.
A fire bolt updates while its next position has no obstacle → The fire bolt sprite occupies a different position between consecutive gameplay frames.
A fire bolt updates while its next position intersects a solid obstacle → The fire bolt sprite disappears from the playfield.
A fire bird updates while inside its patrol range with rightward speed → The fire bird sprite moves right between consecutive gameplay frames.
A fire bird updates at the right edge of its patrol range → The fire bird changes from rightward horizontal motion to leftward horizontal motion on the following gameplay frames.
A fire bird updates at a firing interval during its patrol → A new fire-bolt sprite appears directly below the fire bird.
A volcanic lava actor updates while its next position has no obstacle → The volcanic lava sprite occupies a different position between consecutive gameplay frames.
A volcanic lava actor updates while its next position intersects a solid obstacle → The volcanic lava sprite returns to its original volcano opening position.
A fire tree updates before it has added fruit → Between 4 and 7 berry sprites appear around the fire tree branches.
The air level begins after its generated layout is displayed → The player starts in the lower central area of the playfield and the air gem is visible in the upper central area of the playfield.
The river level begins after its generated layout is displayed → The player starts on a low visible board or platform in the river playfield.
